text:
I built something to fix a problem that's bugged me for years.

Booking a restaurant takes way too many steps — checking their website, calling and hoping someone picks up, digging through social media just to find a number or send a message. So i built Askors — you just chat with it and it books the table for you. One step. English or Tagalog, doesn't matter.

Right now i'm looking for a few restaurants willing to be the first to try it — free while we're still early. If you own a restaurant, or know someone who does, head to website to become a partner.

Curious how it actually works? the website walks you through it — www.askors.com

just want to know when it's live? join the waitlist there too.

And while you're on the site, you'll also see the bigger vision for where Askors is headed.

IG: https://www.instagram.com/askorsai/
aeiou // founder, askors

Our goal has always been simple: **make modern customer retention tools accessible to every Filipino business—not just big brands.**

We believe technology shouldn't be exclusive to enterprises. MSMEs deserve the same tools to build customer loyalty, encourage repeat visits, and grow sustainably.

We're continuously improving the platform based on feedback from real merchants, and we're excited to keep building.

Thanks for having us! 💚

having using orms and writing raw sql queries in the past projects, i strongly recommend for you to try sql query builders with type support instead like kysely. they have the best developer experience same as orms and you get to have full control like writing sql queries in a safe manner

text:
One thing I’d love for us to improve as a community is the quality of what we share.

Whether it’s an app, a launch post, a question, or a showcase, spend naman tayo kahit a few extra minutes lang polishing it. 

With AI tools available today, there’s really no reason to settle for low-effort content anymore.

Using AI is completely fine. I use it every day. But there’s a difference between using AI as a tool and posting slop that hasn’t been reviewed or verified. That's why some of your posts aren't approved din.

The same goes for your apps. If you can’t put in the effort to present or build your own app well, how can you expect other people to put in the effort to download it, test it, or give you meaningful feedback?

Let’s raise the standard together. Better apps attract better feedback. And a higher-quality community benefits every builder here.

🚀 After months of development, I finally launched **Courtzy** on Android and iOS!

It's an app for running open-play sessions in **pickleball, badminton, tennis, and table tennis**.

The idea came from watching organizers juggle paddle stacks, whiteboards, spreadsheets, and group chats just to keep games moving. I wanted to see if I could build something that automates the entire experience.

Some of the features:
* 🎾 Fair player rotation algorithms (Game Count, Time Played, Round Robin, Swiss)
* 📊 Live scoring and player standings
* 🏆 Per-sport Elo ratings & leaderboards
* 📱 Multi-court session management
* 🌐 Offline-first local sessions (no account required)
* ☁️ Live spectator mode & cloud-backed events

Landing page:
[https://courtzy.netlify.app/](https://courtzy.netlify.app/)

I'd love to hear feedback from fellow builders! Also happy to answer technical questions about the architecture or implementation as well. 😊

# Hi, App Builders PH!

I'd like to share a project I've been working on: **Pomogrove, a web-based productivity and study app** designed to help users stay focused while making studying more engaging.

**Current Features**
* Pomodoro Timer
* Streak Tracker & Tree Leveling System
* Flashcards with a spaced repetition algorithm that prioritizes previously missed answers
* Customizable Notepad
## Pomogrove is still under active development, and I'm continuously adding new features and improvements.

If you have a few minutes, I'd appreciate it if you could give Pomogrove a try and share your thoughts. Suggestions, feature ideas, and constructive feedback are always welcome and will help shape future updates.

**Focus. Learn. Grow.**
[https://pomogrove-beta.vercel.app/](https://pomogrove-beta.vercel.app/)

(Looking for Android beta testers)

Meet "Aye-Aye"

Your Private AI Memory OS

PTPA especially kay Bryl Lim , this project is abandoned 2-3 months ago, it was conceptualize nung nagstart yung animal mascot meta, hindi po ito "Tarsier" it's an 'aye-aye' a primate that can only be found on Madagascar. why AYE-AYE because it sounds like "AI-AI"

And now, nagkaroon ng time kaya nabuhay ulit.

What does it do?

You give it permissions to your desired apps, then it will automatically index the screen of your desired app. Meron din itong screenshot indexing that uses OCR.

Ex: Facebook

It will automatically and randomly do snap snapshot indexing.

Why? To be able to recall what you did, what you watched, what you read and etc.

Is it safe? Yes, 100% everything is stored locally. Isang clear data mo lang, burado na po lahat lahat.

Wala po itong any hooks or any API calls.

This app is build for privacy lovers. And I will continue to build more privacy tools.

Video demo below po.

Sa mga interested masubukan yung app.

Maraming salamat.

text:
𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗦𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗺𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝗠𝗶𝗻𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘆: 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗟𝗼𝘃𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 + 𝗦𝘂𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲

I built 𝗖𝗵𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗵 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁, a church management platform for discipleship tracking, member data, and ministry operations using 𝗟𝗼𝘃𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 + 𝗦𝘂𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲.

The build took me three weeks. Testing took four more. Worth every day.

𝗟𝗼𝘃𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗵𝗲𝗹𝗽𝗲𝗱 𝗺𝗲 𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻 𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗮𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗮 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗺. I could describe screens in plain language, iterate quickly, and watch the UI come to life almost instantly. For someone with a bigger vision than budget, it felt like a superpower.

𝗦𝘂𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗣𝗼𝘀𝘁𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗦𝗤𝗟, row level security, real time updates, and multi role authentication already built in. I was able to create secure access for church leaders, members, and admins, each seeing exactly what they need and nothing more.

What started as spreadsheets and scattered records is now becoming a streamlined system designed to help ministry focus more on people, discipleship, and connection.

Grateful as well to [Pastor Joe Poblete](https://web.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100089918995730&__cft__[0]=AZYV1n9Uc2200ST-U660xB5-Z6Y5zm1BoolPTg2pMPg7jD6AApHXi3mltAsTxx8iUA1j_i784MrQVG-zVLUTnniKhzactfGlGdDAioLjidqFJUKqBtIpw9Y2VqMYaOw9tw-b5Ie8GxOG667NJHm2V2h_w1mk490MMDZzbJwpzyNricnv0a1xTUHtWa8urm9u8w5uKbtZcS6OlkrUZzR6qvfD&__tn__=-]K-R) and the team at Victory Tuguegarao for allowing me to test and refine the platform in a real ministry setting. Your trust and feedback helped shape Church Connect into something more practical and impactful.

Need an app for your church or organization? Let’s build something purposeful together.

text:
# **HABI PH**

(Still cooking, Need suggestions, corrections, negative reactions 😂)

I created **HABI PH** (with the use of AI) to give every hardworking Filipino the opportunity to earn through their skills. I believe that many talented workers remain unemployed or underemployed—not because they lack ability, but because they lack access to opportunities.

My goal is to connect skilled workers with people who need their services, helping them build a stable income, strengthen their reputation, and become more self-reliant. Through HABI PH, I hope to empower Filipinos to rely on their skills, improve their quality of life, and reduce dependence on government assistance by creating more opportunities for honest work.

Key Features
* Hyper-local job matching based on your current location.
* One-tap **"Available Today"** status for workers.
* Fast and easy job posting for homeowners and businesses.
* Search nearby skilled workers by trade, location, and availability.
* Two-way ratings and reviews to build trust.
* Transparent daily rate guide to promote fair pricing.
* Direct in-app messaging between workers and clients.
* Verified worker profiles for safer hiring.
* Daily job listings to keep opportunities fresh and relevant.
* Direct payment between workers and clients, with no commission deducted from workers.
* Worker reputation and job history to increase future opportunities.
* Optimized for low-end Android devices with minimal mobile data usage.

**HABI PH — Hanap mo, Trabaho mo.**

[https://hanap-trabaho.vercel.app/](https://hanap-trabaho.vercel.app/)

Another budget tracker for you guys! Haha nagdadalawang isip pako kung tatapusin ko to since every day parang may bagong budget tracker. But this is the first project ive been doing for the past 3 months. Ive made this one tailored on how i do my budgeting. might work for me and for you! 

I need help with 12 testers for 14 days 🙏
join the group link first -> 
[https://groups.google.com/g/obelus-testers](https://groups.google.com/g/obelus-testers)

the install the app -> 
[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.obelus.app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.obelus.app)

Thank you peeps! 

**Built with 🛠️**
* **Flutter** (Dart) — one codebase, Android + iOS
* **Riverpod** for state, **Drift/SQLite** for local-first storage (your data stays on-device)
* **Claude (Haiku/Sonnet)** for the chat + analysis, **Gemini** for categorization and Logging reaction
* **Cloudflare Workers** as proxies for the AI + market-price APIs (keys server-side, cached)
* **fl_chart** for the graphs

text:
I am beyond thrilled to finally unveil **Zapurr** 

For the past **2 months**, I’ve been working on **a comprehensive pet care and community safety app dedicated to stray cats and dogs** with the goal of **streamlining their health management while building a proactive, near real-time support network for animals in need.**

 Whether you're looking to **effortlessly track daily meals and medications, organize vet records, or instantly locate life-saving blood donors**, this platform keeps you connected with critical push notifications for everything from routine check-ins to urgent stray sightings and lost pet alerts.

You can check it out here for more features: https://zapurr.com/

I’d love to hear your thoughts, feedback, or any questions you have. 

Note: The app is currently in the final stages of the app review process.

text:
🚶‍♀️ 𝗦𝗮𝗳𝗲 𝗯𝗮 '𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗴 𝗱𝗮𝗱𝗮𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗻 𝗸𝗼?

Kung isa ka sa mga taong ilang beses nang nagtanong nito bago umuwi, lalo na sa gabi, hindi ka nag-iisa.

Maraming commuters ang napipilitang mag-isip kung aling ruta ang mas ligtas, maghintay ng makakasabay, o magmadaling maglakad sa madidilim na bahagi ng kalsada. Para sa marami, hindi lang oras at pamasahe ang iniisip sa pag-commute—kasama rin ang personal na kaligtasan.

𝗞𝗮𝘆𝗮 𝗻𝗶𝗹𝗮𝗹𝗮𝘆𝗼𝗻 𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗮𝘀 𝗺𝗮𝘂𝗻𝗮𝘄𝗮𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗴𝗮 𝗸𝗮𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗮𝘀𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗮 𝗽𝗮𝗺𝗮𝗺𝗮𝗴𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗻 𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁.

👋 𝗠𝗮𝗴𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘄!

Kami ay mga 1st Year Computer Science students mula sa Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP). Kasalukuyan kaming gumagawa ng isang project na nakatuon sa pagpapabuti ng commuting experience at pakiramdam ng kaligtasan ng mga commuter sa paligid ng Sta. Mesa.

Bago namin ito ipagpatuloy, nais muna naming makinig sa mga totoong karanasan ng mga taong araw-araw na bumibiyahe. Hindi ito para magbenta o mag-promote ng anumang produkto—bahagi lamang ito ng aming research.

𝗡𝗮𝗴𝗵𝗮𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗽 𝗸𝗮𝗺𝗶 𝗻𝗴:
• 👩 Babaeng commuters

text:
Hey everyone! Share ko lang itong small npm package 😅

Every time I start a new web app, I end up doing the same PWA setup manually, adding the manifest, configuring service workers, handling push notifications, and creating install prompts and and building the UI from scratch.

After doing it over and over, I decided to package everything into a reusable npm package.

So I built **pwa-notifications -** a zero-config, framework-agnostic toolkit that handles the tedious parts of setting up PWAs and web push notifications.

It helps with:
* Service worker setup
* Manifest generation
* VAPID key support
* Cross-platform install prompts (instructions only in iOS Safari)
* Fully customizable UI components like install banners, settings blocks, and custom prompt dialogs

Getting started is as simple as: **`npm install pwa-notifications`**

Would love for you to give it a try! Feedback, suggestions are always welcome.

🔗Docs: [https://dev-reymark.github.io/pwa-notifications](https://dev-reymark.github.io/pwa-notifications)

🔗Link: [https://appbuildersph.com/apps/pwa-push-notifications](https://appbuildersph.com/apps/pwa-push-notifications)

text:
Hello guys! You got 5 mins to read? 

website: https://www.learnagaru.com/
instagram: https://www.instagram.com/learnagaru/
download link: https://apps.apple.com/ph/app/agaru-learn-japanese/id6776997348

I just wanted to share an app I made called Agaru. If you’re learning Japanese and want something to help you practice and retain what you’ve learned, feel free to check it out.

Honestly, it started as a personal thing. I just wanted a tool for myself to learn kana without the usual grind. Using my own method inside the app, I somehow got both Hiragana and Katakana down in about 2 days. The retention genuinely surprised me — that’s when I thought, okay, maybe this isn’t just for me.

Around the same time, I kept seeing TikTok contents of learners juggling 4–5 different apps just to get all the features they need — one for kana, one for kanji, one for grammar, another for listening. App-hopping is a hassle. And a lot of those apps lock the useful stuff behind a monthly subscription.

I get that servers cost money, but monthly fees kind of defeat the purpose when Nihongo is a long journey. If you’re a student or just starting out in life, paying every month while learning at your own pace adds pressure you don’t really need.

So I built Agaru for people who are actually serious about learning. I approached it like a gamified learning app and more like a productivity app — something to keep the fire burning, because with Japanese, consistency is really the only thing that works.

Let me run down what’s already inside 

Decks

* Vocab and Kanji decks organized by JLPT level, from N5 to N1. Each level comes with ready-made decks: Greetings, Numbers, Days & Time, Family, Food & Drink, Places, Common Verbs, Adjectives, and more.

* Browse Words / Browse Kanji — flip through everything and add any word or kanji to your study set with one tap.

* Create your own deck — build custom sets from scratch and load in whatever you’re focusing on.

* Decks can also be used as audio cards. Yep! You can play them in the background while doing other things.

A quick look at the rest:

* Kana and Kanji Table with actual tracing — a full Hiragana and Katakana reference, including basic characters, dakuon, combinations, and more.

* Muscle Memory drills — timed Kana Guessing and staged Reading Sessions that keep bringing your missed items back until they stick.

* Grammar — Genki and Tobira-based lessons from N5 to N1 in a guided card flow, with particles and nouns color-coded so the structure stands out. Plus, there’s a Grammar Quiz to test yourself.

* Speaking practice — hear a word, say it, and get scored on your pronunciation.

* Listen mode — play a deck hands-free, set the repeat count, and choose your preferred voice and speed.

* Stay-consistent tools — daily reminders, streaks, and a built-in Pomodoro timer.

* Works offline — study on the train, on a plane, or wherever you are.

* Sensei Chatbot via Apple Intelligence

* Widgets

* And more…

I’m pro-education, but let’s be real — when something is completely free, people often don’t value it. A small price creates commitment.

text:

Welcome to Elixir world! :) I started with documentation then Pragmatic studio (I got a discount code from Vince, a couple of years ago)

text:
Hey everyone! I built a little app called Penny and wanted to share it here.

It's a subscription tracker for Mac and iPhone. Basically, I kept forgetting about random subscriptions charging my card every month, so I built something to fix that for myself, then figured other people probably deal with the same thing.

Kept it minimal on purpose. No clutter, no dashboards full of stuff you don't need. You add a subscription, it shows you what's coming up and when, and there's a little widget so you can glance at your next bill without even opening the app. That's pretty much it.

The free version tracks up to 3 subscriptions. If you've got more than that, there's a one-time ₱199 unlock for unlimited subscriptions plus some analytics. No recurring fee, no subscription to track your subscriptions (the irony would kill me).

Would love any feedback if you try it out, good or bad. Still very early days and I'm the only one working on it.

text: Ask ko lang, whats the process and cost of registering our apps to the BIR?

topComments.text:
Basically, hindi yung apps ang i-reregister. It's the business. 

If sole proprietor ka, meaning, mag-isa lang sa business, you can register sa BIR as either Self-employed (freelancer). 

Pero suggested sa ganito is to register as SOLE PROPRIETOR. Meaning, may business trade name ka. You have to register with DTI first. Para makuha yung trade name. 

For example, ABC Business Solutions. 
Then that will be your business name. 

It doesn't have to be the product name. 
Parang Google by Alphabet. Google ang app. Alphabet yung company name. 

So after you register sa DTI, you need to register sa BIR. 
Get your Invoice, Manual books of account, and ultimately, get your COR. Certificate of registration.

As to cost, nagdedepende sya sa ilang factors, if maghihire ka ng accountant/firm, or DIY mo sya. Siguro all in all 5k to 15k. 

Sa BIR documents (roughly 3k to 4k). Pero iba pa yung mga mayor's permit and other fees you have to prepare. 

Then if magpapalakad ka sa mga nagpprocess, you have to pay for their service fee. 

Pero kung corporation ang want mo, you have to register as a corporation sa BIR. Meron rin SEC registration na need asikasuhin. 

Like sa case ko, I am currently building a tax compliance app (bookkeeping/accounting/tax), ongoing development na kami. And registered sya as sole proprietor. Different ang business name nya. 

Soon, hopefully mailagay na rin namin dito ang app namin. 💛

Not to mention po, once registered, the monthly and quarterly, and annual reports, may earnings man o wala... And also the penalties and open cases if hindi nakapag comply...

And hindi na operating ang business, needed po na i-officially close... Or else, will be faced again with all the penalties and open cases... Huhu... 

I wish sana may easier way to have all of these na hindi hassle... Para mapag focus lang sa app development...

text:
Hey everyone, student dev here.

I finally shipped KursoKo, a free career guidance web app for Filipino students (especially SHS).

I started this about a year ago as a personal side project. Idea was simple: something like the personality quizzes people love, but pointed at course + career direction for the Philippines. I wasn’t even sure good PH-focused career assessment tools existed, so I tried building one.

The product part was easier than the data.
Gathering and validating schools, scholarships, and career mappings took most of the time. That’s why it sat unfinished for a while.

What it does now: 
• Short career-interest quiz (~10 min, no sign-up)
• Career matches + course direction
• Top schools per career path
• Scholarships matched to those paths
• 59 careers · 227 schools · 304 scholarships (still growing)

Who it’s for: students figuring out course, school, and scholarships before college apps. Not a founder tool, but I’m sharing here because this community actually ships.

Would love feedback from builders: 
• UX on results flow
• Anything broken on mobile
• If you know PH schools/scholarships missing from the data

🔗 Live app: https://kurso-ko.vercel.app/

📌 Listing: https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/kursoko

Thanks for keeping this group about real builds. Happy to answer questions.

text:
Hi App Builders PH! 👋

I'm a 2nd year BSIT student, and I want to share my **first real personal project**: **Bentolink** (bentolink.win), a link-in-bio built specifically for Filipinos.

**The problem I wanted to solve:**
Most creators and sellers here use Linktree, but it's just a cold list of blue links, and it doesn't fit how we actually earn. Walang GCash, walang Shopee/TikTok Shop, walang rate card. So I built one that does.

**What Bentolink is:**
A bento-grid link page with tiles made for the PH:
* 💸 GCash tile (QR or number) so buyers pay you directly
* 🛒 Shopee & TikTok Shop tiles
* ⭐ Rate card in pesos, so brands stop asking "magkano?"
* 💬 Messenger one-tap link
* 📊 Analytics (views + which links get tapped)
* 🎨 Drag-and-drop builder with themes, no code needed

It's also aimed at gaming communities and private servers who want a shareable hub (downloads, Discord, GCash donations) without running a website.

Self-hosted on a Hetzner VPS via Coolify (Docker), behind Cloudflare. Sobrang dami kong natutunan dito, especially sa deployment and hardening side.

**What I'm hoping for:**
Honest feedback po. 🙏 Design, UX, features, pricing, kahit anong "bakit ganito?" Try mo gumawa ng sarili mong page (free forever ang core, may 7-day Premium trial) and tell me what breaks or what's confusing.

👉 Try it: https://appbuildersph.com/apps/bentolink
Focused on **web-only** for now (works great on mobile browsers), with **Android and iOS apps coming soon**.

(Bonus: may isa pa akong project, **Skirmix** (skirmix.xyz), a free esports tracker for Valorant/PUBG/Dota2, in case gusto niyo rin tingnan.)

Salamat po, and I'd really appreciate any support or feedback. 🧡

Hello again, AppBuildersPH! 👋

A while back, I shared the launch of my indie game, Recalled, with this community. I'm happy to share that it's now reached 2,000+ downloads on Google Play! 🎉

Since then, I've continued working on updates and recently added new game modes, including Toon Match—a mode where you try to recreate the colors of familiar cartoon, game, and pop culture characters entirely from memory. It's surprisingly challenging, and if your color matching is way off... the game isn't afraid to roast you for it. 😂

Recalled is all about testing different kinds of memory through quick, unique mini-games, and I'm still actively improving it based on player feedback.

If you haven't had the chance to try it yet, I'd really appreciate it if you could check it out. As always, I'd love to hear your thoughts or suggestions from fellow builders!

text:
I started building ComicShelf last April just to track my own comic collection, and it kind of got out of hand in the best way possible.

What started as a personal project turned into a full-blown app that I have been pouring my heart into for the past 2 months. It began simple, just me wanting a clean way to log my comics, but one feature led to another and here we are.

Here is what ComicShelf can do now:

*Track your comics, manga, manhwa, webtoons, manhua, and light novels with cover art, progress tracking, ratings, and personal notes.

*Add movies, TV shows, anime, mini-series, and documentaries to your Watchlist, complete with runtime, genre, and IMDb ratings.

*Follow the full reading and watching order of major universes like the MCU, DCU, One Piece, Attack on Titan, Star Wars, and more on the Timeline tab.

*Share what you are currently reading or watching directly from the app, because good stories are worth talking about.

*Earn achievements, track your streaks, and get a Spotify Wrapped-style Stats summary of your reading and watching habits.

It's free, it works on mobile, and it has been one of the most rewarding things I have ever built. If you are into comics, manga, anime, or movies, give it a shot. I would love to hear what you think.

Y’all can try it here:

www.comicshelf.online
https://appbuildersph.com/apps/comicshelf

## **If you’re not sure what solo activities to do, I’ve built an app for you**

Hi guys, solo dev here

I built an app called Questle because minsan gusto ko lumabas or gumawa ng something alone, pero wala akong maisip besides the usual:
* cafe
* lakad
* doomscroll
* repeat until character development / organic encounter happens

Questle is basically a solo side-quest app. It gives you small solo activity ideas you can do, then you can log the ones you completed with notes, mood, and photos.

Parang tiny quest tracker for your solo activities and it also gives you daily quests suggestions.

The idea is simple:
* open the app
* check your daily solo activity quest
* do the thing
* log it as a memory
* slowly build your own little trail of solo experiences

First release / beta-ish version pa siya, so I’d really appreciate honest feedback, bug reports, or feature requests.

Site/app:
[[https://questle.org](https://questle.org)](https://questle.org)

[https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/questle](https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/questle)

Hello everyone.

I'm a developer and fitness enthusiast, and I am incredibly excited to introduce my latest project, **Pace Mentor**.

Here is a breakdown of the core functionalities I have recently engineered:
* **Tailored Endurance Blueprints:** The application architects bespoke running programs calibrated precisely to an individual’s current physiological profile. This dynamic system is engineered to help newcomers establish sustainable habits while empowering competitive athletes to shatter their personal milestones.
* **Live Metrics & Predictive Analytics:** The moment you hit the pavement, the platform monitors your splits and delivers deep-dive performance summaries. Runners can leverage these data-driven insights to visualize exactly how their velocity and stride efficiency evolve over time.
* **Adaptive AI Consultation:** To maintain user momentum, the system features a round-the-clock automated trainer. Moving far beyond traditional distance logging, it acts as an interactive virtual strategist—delivering elite-level athletic guidance without the overhead of a private physical coach.
> 

**An architectural note on the interface:** You may notice the UI/UX leans toward a minimalist aesthetic. I am strictly optimizing this entire APK to maintain a featherweight system footprint across all mobile chipsets. Eliminating resource-heavy animations and complex graphic wrappers ensures zero background latency during active GPS and workout tracking. My immediate priority is flawless code execution and the mathematical precision of the running structures. Thank you for your understanding.

Pace Mentor is actively in its development phase, and I am continuously refining its architecture. I would highly value your professional feedback, technical insights, or feature recommendations to help elevate this platform further.

Thank you for your time and for supporting independent development!

text:
Hi everyone 👋
I’d like to share something I’ve been building and would really appreciate your feedback.

I created Mnemra 🧠, an AI workspace that helps customer support agents, VAs, founders, and small teams preserve and reuse their support knowledge.

A common problem I’ve noticed is that support knowledge gets scattered everywhere:

📄 Old tickets
📝 Google Docs
💬 Slack or chat threads
📚 SOPs and FAQs
🌐 Help center pages or public docs
🧑‍💻 Things only one teammate remembers

Then when the same issue happens again, the team has to search manually or solve it from scratch. Not exactly the peak of civilization.

That’s what Mnemra is trying to fix.

With Mnemra, you can upload your existing support materials like PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV, and Markdown files, paste old support conversations, or let it crawl public web pages such as help centers, docs, FAQs, and knowledge base articles. 🌐

After that, you can ask questions and get answers based on the knowledge you added, with sources so you can verify where the answer came from. 🔎

What makes Mnemra different is that it is not trying to replace your support team or force you into a full helpdesk setup. It is built more like a support memory layer that works with the knowledge you already have, even if it’s messy, scattered, inside files, pasted conversations, or existing public pages.

Most tools focus on structured knowledge bases, customer-facing chatbots, or big company workflows. Mnemra is focused on helping individuals, VAs, small teams, and growing support teams quickly reuse their own support history without needing a complicated setup first.

The goal is simple:

⚡ Answer customer questions faster
🧠 Preserve support knowledge
🌐 Turn existing web pages into searchable knowledge
🚀 Help new team members onboard easier
🔁 Avoid solving the same issue again and again
📌 Keep useful fixes even when people leave

You can check it here:
https://mnemra.tyvera.app/

Follow the page for updates:
Mnemra

This is still an early version, so feedback would really mean a lot. I’d love to know what feels useful, what feels unclear, and what features or integrations would make this more valuable for real support workflows.

If you know someone working in customer support, VA work, SaaS, operations, or any role where they handle repeated customer questions, feel free to share this with them too 🙏

Thank you so much.

text:
Learning with AI or Tutorial Videos/Websites as an Incoming First-Year BSCS Student
Greetings, I would like to know your opinions regarding this matter kasi nowadays madali nalang mag build ng app with AI.

I'm currently learning with Claude wherein sinasabi ko po kung anong feature or function yung nasa isip ko and pinapa break down ko po sakanya yung bawat line of code.

Mas okay pa rin po ba mag study from scratch or integrate na po ang AI sa pag aral? Since malaking leverage na po ngayon ang maalam sa pag orchestrate ng AI.

Thank you in advance!

topComments.text: I suggest learning from scratch before using AI. That's really how you build confidence din kasi.

Learn the fundamentals first. AI's output still depends heavily on the developer using it. The more knowledgeable you are and the better you understand what you're building, the more effective AI becomes.

Even with Antigravity's lower-end model, I'm still able to generate high-quality code, design proper architectures, and follow solid engineering principles. AI is a tool. It amplifies your skills, not replaces them.

Okay this is officially live on the Play Store now 😭🎉

Eskwela — the schedule app that turns a photo of your class schedule into a clean, organized calendar. No retyping, no manual entry. Just snap it and you're done.

Get reminders before every class, a home screen widget so your next class is always one glance away, and dark mode because we see you studying at 2am.

If you're still manually typing your schedule into your phone every semester, there's a faster way now.

Try it. Your future self during finals week will thank you.
Link in the comments 👇
Video demonstration below the post

text:
Hello everyone.

I'm Fhiej Dale, a first-year BSIT student. I would like to share my project called Blood Map PH.

Here are some of the latest features I've added:

 Verification System (Prototype) – Users must first be verified before they can create a blood donor or blood request pin on the map. This feature is still a prototype and will continue to be improved.

 Blood Map Card with QR Code (Prototype) – Once verified, users receive a digital Blood Map card with a unique QR code. Anyone can scan the QR code to view the user's Blood Map profile. This feature is also still a prototype.

Location Obfuscation – To help protect user privacy, the app no longer displays users' exact locations on the map. Instead, it only shows a generalized location, making it possible to find nearby donors or blood requests without exposing precise coordinates.

I also want to apologize if the UI/UX design isn't as polished as it could be. I'm building this entire project using only my Android phone, so adding too many animations, visual effects, or complex UI elements can make my device lag and slow down development. For now, I'm focusing more on the functionality and core features of the application. Thank you for your understanding.

Blood Map PH is still under development, and I'm continuously learning and improving it. I would greatly appreciate any feedback or suggestions that could help make the project better.

Thank you for taking the time to check out my project. I truly appreciate your support! 

Try it here: https://bloodmappin.vercel.app/

I built a **verifiable bulk certificate generator** that also solves certificate distribution.

This is a feature inside **Dasig.org** to help volunteer clubs and NGOs issue certificates after every activity. Then I realized the same workflow is used by **teachers**, **schools**, **government agencies**, and **community organizers**, so I released it as a standalone tool.

I didn't want to replace Canva. People already design great certificates there.

Instead, I integrated the **Canva Connect API**. Connect your Canva template, and Dasig handles the rest.

* Generate up to 500 personalized certificates in seconds.
* Add dynamic fields with a drag-and-drop editor.
* Share one self-serve certificate registry instead of sending certificates one by one.
* Verify instantly through a QR code.
* Verified organizations earn the Dasig Verified badge for trusted credentials.

No sign up required for browser generation. Sign in to save your cert templates, registry link and add future batches, and access to server generation.

I hope this saves organizers hours of manual work after every event.

Free Bulk Certificate Generator with QR Verification: [https://dasig.org/certificate-generator](https://dasig.org/certificate-generator)

text:
For tech and media teams tired of Alt-Tabbing while live.

Just want to share **OBS Controller**, a lightweight remote dashboard I made for OBS Studio. You can use it on an Android phone, another laptop, or a Windows device as long as it is connected to the same network.

Useful if:
* You only have one monitor
* You are using a laptop and need to minimize OBS for other tasks
* You want to switch scenes using an Android phone or another laptop
* You want to let another person control scenes, sources, streaming, or recording
* Your media team needs a simple mobile-friendly OBS control panel

Features:
* Switch OBS scenes
* Use Studio Mode with Preview and Program view
* Show or hide sources per scene
* Activate or deactivate camera sources
* Mute or unmute audio sources
* View live OBS preview
* Start or stop streaming
* Start or stop recording
* See live stream or recording timer
* Real-time OBS updates using WebSocket
* Saves host and port settings for faster connection
* Works on the same local network  

Requirements:
* Latest OBS Studio with WebSocket Server Settings
* Recent Android version
* Windows 10/11
* Devices must be connected to the same local network

Free download link in the comment section.

[https://obs-controller-app.web.app/](https://obs-controller-app.web.app/)

text:
Hello fellow builders! 

Just wanted to share a small win.

A few days ago, I shared TindaDone here and in a few communities. I honestly didn't expect much, so I was surprised to see multiple people already start the free trial.

For those who haven't seen it yet, TindaDone is an offline-first business management app built for sari-sari stores and small businesses. It helps with:

 Sales Tracking
 Inventory Management
 Utang Records
 Expense Tracking
 Daily Reports

It's still very early, and there's still a lot I want to improve—from onboarding to the overall experience—but seeing real people try something you built is a different kind of motivation.

I'm also grateful to be part of the AppBuilders community. Seeing everyone build, experiment, and ship their ideas has been incredibly inspiring.

Thank you to everyone who checked out TindaDone and shared feedback. Every comment and suggestion genuinely helps.

Still building. Still learning. Still shipping. 

If you'd like to support TindaDone, you can also upvote it here:
 [https://appbuildersph.com/apps/tindadone]

text:
**Meet Apex JS: the full-stack, AI-native meta-framework for Alpine.js.**

Apex is to Alpine what Next.js is to React: file-based routing, server rendering, islands, components, and a typed data layer over Drizzle (SQLite/Postgres/Turso/Neon).

Then it does something no other framework does — every typed API route is *also* a live MCP tool. Write one `defineApexRoute`, get a REST endpoint **and** a tool your AI can call. No extra library, no drift. One definition, two surfaces.

→ HTML on first paint, real SEO, ship almost zero JS
→ Point Claude at `/mcp` and it can operate your app
→ Scaffold and run in under a minute

Build your first **Apex JS** App: **npm i -g @apex-stack/core**
Website + Docs: https://apexjs.site/
Github Repo: https://github.com/andrecorugda/apexjs

Working framework, MIT, built in the open. Demo below 👇

#framework

#alpinejs

#fullstack

I created HeyDenta is an AI receptionist for  dental clinics. Built after watching a real clinic lose after-hours inquiries that should have been bookings.

Core

🦷 Answers patient chats and calls 24/7, Taglish-friendly

🔁 Follows up with patients overdue for a check-up

💸 Priced in Philippine pesos

Under the hood

🚦 Multi-tenant with per-clinic guardrails on every prompt

🧪 Each tweak auto-tested: happy paths, jailbreaks, refusals, tenant isolation

📡 24/7 monitoring with auto-retry webhooks and alerts

✋ Money and clinical actions always need a human confirm

My ops layer:

🔍 Weekly log sweep: root cause traced, fix prepared, ships on one approval word

📝 Docs self-audit monthly against the shipping code

🧠 Risky changes get second opinions from independent models before shipping

🎬 Marketing graphics and demo videos auto-produced and queued

🚪 One rule everywhere: money and patient data wait for a human tap

Hello, App Builders! 👋 I posted my app here before when it was still in closed testing. I'm excited to share that it is now officially LIVE on Google Play and FREE to download! Test it out with your barkadas! 🚀

- - - - - - 

"𝘞𝘢𝘭𝘢 𝘱𝘢 '𝘬𝘰𝘯𝘨 𝘤𝘢𝘴𝘩, 𝘱𝘢-𝘢𝘣𝘰𝘯𝘰 𝘮𝘶𝘯𝘢 𝘢𝘩?" 😅💸

We’ve all been there. You go on a fun barkada trip, grab dinner, or split the rent—and one person ends up paying for everything first. Then comes the real headache: figuring out exactly who owes who without making things awkward. 📉

text:
I recently shared a code review prompt in a developer community.

It ended up getting 52 likes, 42 comments and a few shares, but the comments taught me far more than the prompt itself.

Reading through the discussion, I realized I had met almost every personality you’ll run into in tech.

The Drive-By Dismisser: Someone who came in with, “You’re ignorant if you think otherwise.” The delivery wasn’t great, but underneath it was a valid point.

What I learned: Try to separate the message from the tone. You don’t have to respond to the insult, just the idea.

The Credential Warrior: Almost every reply started with, “I get paid to do this.” Many of the technical points were actually correct.

What I learned: Experience matters, but it’s even more helpful to understand why something works. Good explanations teach more than titles ever can.

The One-Upper: “You’re about a year behind.” 😅 Then they shared a really thoughtful agentic workflow.

What I learned: It’s easy to get distracted by comparisons, but sometimes there’s genuine value hidden behind them. Their workflow didn’t replace my evaluation prompt. It complemented it.

The Precision Editor: Pointed out that asking an AI to “suggest a better approach” for every issue can encourage it to invent unnecessary fixes.

This ended up being my favorite piece of feedback.

We eventually agreed that it’s often better to split the work into separate passes. First identify problems, then suggest improvements. One goal per completion.

My biggest takeaway wasn’t about prompting. It was about conversations.

Kindness doesn’t automatically make someone right, and a harsh tone doesn’t automatically make someone wrong.

As the original poster, I also noticed something interesting. The tone of each conversation often followed my reply, not the original comment.

Acknowledge good points quickly. Ask clear questions. Don’t mirror hostility.

Because when you post in a public community, you’re rarely just talking to one person. There are hundreds, or even thousands, of people quietly reading, learning, and forming an impression based on how everyone handles the discussion.

Sometimes the comment section feels like the workplace with the politeness filter turned off.

And honestly, that’s not always a bad place to learn.

#SoftwareEngineering #PromptEngineering #AI #TechCommunity

Just listed LETPass on the App Builders PH directory and I'd love your honest eyes on it. 🦅

Link: [https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/letpass](https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/letpass)

Quick backstory: I looked into what LET (Licensure Exam for Teachers) review centers charge here in PH, and it's expensive. For a lot of aspiring teachers, that cost is the wall between them and passing. So I built LETPass, an AI-powered LET review platform, priced for students instead of gatekeeping them.

What's inside:
* Full question bank aligned to actual exam coverage (Gen Ed, Prof Ed, Specialization)
* Timed mock exams that simulate the real thing
* Performance analytics that show exactly which competencies need work
* Gabby, an AI tutor (a chibi Philippine eagle, from the Filipino word gabay) who explains every answer and adapts to your weak areas

It's freemium: free trial and credits to start, then an affordable Exam Cycle Pass (PHP 99 to 249) instead of a recurring subscription, since LET is seasonal.

I'm a solo builder and still far from my full vision, so I'd genuinely value:
1. Your gut reaction to the listing page itself. Does it make you want to click through?
2. If you (or someone you know) is taking the LET, try it and tell me what's missing.
3. An upvote on the directory would mean a lot as I'm just getting traction. 🙏

Salamat, App Builders PH! Building this for Filipino teachers, one exam cycle at a time. 🇵🇭

PTPA
Been building this on my own for a while and I think it's finally at a point where I can let other people try it.

It's called Seatmate.

It's a study app made for Filipino students that works completely offline. No account, no ads, and your data stays on your phone.

The idea came from wanting something that felt less like another productivity app and more like the seatmate you always had in class. That's where Ella comes in. Every time you log a quiz, she responds in natural Taglish. It's a small thing, but I wanted the app to feel a little more human.

Right now you can keep track of your subjects, quizzes, grades, and notes in one place.

It's still an MVP, so it's not on the Play Store yet. I'm a solo student developer and the store fees can wait until I'm sure people actually 

find it useful.

You can download it here:

https://seatmate-site.vercel.app

I have a lot planned for it. I want it to eventually help students review, stay consistent, and feel a little less alone when studying.

If you try it, I'd really appreciate any feedback. Doesn't matter if it's positive or brutal. I'd rather hear what's wrong and make it better than assume it's already good.

And if you're a developer, designer, or just someone who likes building things that help students, feel free to reach out. I'd love to meet more people working on this kind of stuff.

https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/seatmate-gzq

text:
Hello po. First time sharing my mobile web app project called **SariSari**. It is an *offline-first mobile assistant and management application* para po sa mga Filipino sari-sari store owners. Tinutulungan nito ang mga sari-sari store owners na magtrack ng inventory/stocks, magrecord ng sales, pati na rin ang utang ni suki ng hindi na kailangan ng internet. 

## ✨ **Core Features **

**⚡Fast Point of Sales (POS)**: 
* Quick counter sales registering cash or credit (*utang*) transactions. Updates inventory automatically and logs movement records in real time.

**📦 Inventory & Category Tracker:**
* Complete catalog of products, categories, stock counts, selling prices, and purchase costs (calculating margin/markup). Supports low-stock thresholds and alerts

**📓 Suki Credit Ledger (Utang)**:
* Customer registry tracking outstanding suki loans.

**📊 Reports:**
* Dashboard view tracking daily revenue, profitability, inventory valuation, cash vs. credit breakdowns, fast/slow-moving goods, credit aging buckets, and actionable store tips.

**✈️ Offline-First by Default:**
* Inventory CRUD, sales recording, utang tracking, and reports all work end-to-end with airplane mode on. There is no automatic backup yet — keep your device backed up to the cloud through your phone's normal channels.

May ilang parts pa pong either tatapusin or hindi na (reason is sa dami na rin pong similar app idea ng sari-sari management so baka hindi ko na rin ituloy hahaha), but the starting progress of the app is around 5 months ago na. Open po for suggestions, honest feedback, and constructive critism about my app. Salamat po sa platform to share my mobile app even though it is in the development phase.

# **Rescuenect is in App Builders now!**

Rescuenect is a disaster preparedness and community safety application designed to help individuals stay informed and respond quickly during emergencies. It provides real-time weather conditions and the latest earthquake updates, allowing users to monitor potential hazards in their area.

The app enables users to share their current status with the community, report and mark danger zones on an interactive map, and receive important notifications about disasters and safety alerts. Rescuenect also helps users find the nearest and safest evacuation center through intelligent route guidance, ensuring faster and safer evacuation during emergencies.

To support effective communication, the app provides quick access to official government emergency contact numbers, making it easier for users to reach the appropriate authorities when assistance is needed.

Rescuemect is built for residents, communities, emergency responders, and local government units who need a reliable platform for disaster awareness, communication, and emergency response.

ChordOrbit is a music theory practice app for musicians, students, worship teams. It helps you explore chords, scales, modes, family chords, substitutions, progressions, the circle of fifths, piano voicings, guitar positions, standard notation, tuner, and metronome in one clean app.

You can hear chords, view them on piano or guitar, build chord progressions, reorder them, and practice with real-time visual feedback. It also works as an installable PWA, so you can use it on mobile or desktop.

text:
Hello App Builders Community. Hope you're doing well. 

Free tool for anyone studying IELTS Writing. Built this with an IELTS teacher, for the needs of students and the wider community.

Most IELTS prep out there teaches paraphrasing as memorisation. Learn a template, learn a vocabulary list, hope it fits the question on exam day. Examiners see through that fast, and it caps how high your score can go.

What actually raises your score is being able to say the same idea in different ways, quickly, under time pressure. That's a skill you build through practice, not a list you memorise.

So we built Skaldris (https://www.skaldris.com/). You get a real sentence, you rewrite it yourself, and it shows you a model answer plus the exact technique used. Synonym swap, passive voice, nominalisation, and so on.

Over 800 practice sentences across 21 topics. Full Task 1 and Task 2 writing guide. Everything free, no login needed.

This is Phase 1. Kindly recommend it to your friends who are studying for IELTS too. We would really appreciate your feedback, what's confusing, what's missing, what you'd want next.

text:
Hi everyone, I’d like to ask for advice from people who have experience building or launching apps in the Philippines.

I’m currently building a private resort booking and reservation management app for resort owners.

For Phase 1, it’s not yet a public marketplace. It’s mainly a tool for resort owners to manage their bookings. Each private resort is booked as one whole property, so there’s no separate inventory for rooms or amenities.

Current features include a booking calendar, unique booking link for each resort, customer booking form, payment instructions, proof-of-payment upload, date blocking, and simple internal reports.

The app does not process payments. Customers pay the resort owner directly. It also does not issue official invoices or receipts.

But once I onboard enough resort owners, Phase 2 will be the consumer side similar to Airbnb or Agoda, but focused only on private resorts, where users can find and book nearby available resorts easily.

My questions are:

1. For Phase 1, what category would this app fall under in the Philippines? Is it considered SaaS, SPM, booking software, or something else?

2.Since it doesn’t process payments or issue receipts/invoices, what BIR requirements should I prepare for?

3. What legal documents should I prepare before launch? Terms, Privacy Policy, Resort Owner Agreement, etc.?

4.Since customers will submit booking details and upload proof of payment, what should I prepare for Data Privacy compliance?

5.Before Phase 2 becomes a public marketplace, what registrations, permits, or legal risks should I prepare for?

Would really appreciate any advice from anyone who has built or registered something similar. I just want to make sure I’m doing this properly before scaling. Thank you!

Gusto ko talaga na dapat presentable ang lahat ng bagay. To the best of my current ability, I present Chamly to you!! 
Let me know kung may makita kayong something...

I always wanted to be part of something big/cool/unique, and if given a chance, I am open to collaborate. 💻

I am excited sa 1st meet up SOON!

🐾 **Calling Pet Parents: Please Help Me Test VetCheck!**

I am inviting everyone to become early testers for **VetCheck**, a new pet health app designed to make managing your pet’s medical information simpler, safer, and more organized.

VetCheck is your **digital pet health card. An app **built for modern pet owners who want one easy place to keep track of their pet’s care.

With VetCheck, you can:

✅ Safeguard your pet’s medical logs
✅ Track booster and vaccination due dates
✅ Keep important health records in one place
✅ Generate travel-ready pet health summaries
✅ Use an AI-powered medical timeline to better organize your pet’s care history

I'm currently looking for **Android users** to test the app through Google Play and share honest feedback before the official launch.

**How to join as a tester:**
1. Join our Google Group here by scanning the QR code on the right side of the poster.
2. Use the **same email address** connected to your Google Play account.
3. Once your email is added to the tester list, you’ll be able to access VetCheck on Google Play. I will send you the google play link once email is added OR scan the smaller QR code at the middle of the poster.

Your feedback will help us improve the app, fix issues, and make VetCheck more useful for real pet parents and their pets.

🐶🐱 **Interested in helping shape the future of pet health management? Join the tester group today.**

Thank you for supporting VetCheck and helping us build a better experience for pets and their families.

text:
**Sertipikeyt — Generate certificates in minutes, not hours.**

I'm currently building **Sertipikeyt**, a desktop application that simplifies certificate creation and batch generation for schools, organizations, companies, and event organizers.

Instead of editing certificates one by one, Sertipikeyt lets you:
* Design your certificate layout once.
* Define editable fields such as Name, Course, Date, and Certificate Number.
* Import recipient data from Excel or CSV.
* Generate hundreds of personalized certificates in a single process.
* Export certificates as PNG, PDF, or ZIP.

The goal is to make certificate generation simple, fast, and completely offline.

Still under development, and I'm continuously adding new features and improving the experience.

Feedback and suggestions are always welcome.

-

Hi guys,  I've created an app na pang create ng Filipino voiceover (tagalog only for now), for reels, stories etc. 

I use gemni tts at the backend, but my app 

- makes the UI very simple, even your lola can use it
- Ive added phoneme for commonly mispronounced tagalog words
- allows you to set prosody tone etc

Its still in beta/testing stage and Im gathering user feedbacks sa mga content creators.

url: https://pinoyvo.com

text:
Hi mga ka-builder! 👋 

Silent na taga-masid lang ko dito group and I find it inspiring na makita ang ideas turned to apps/platforms and I always aimed to have my own. Ilang buwan kong na-work itong side project, ni-launch ko na finally.

**Ambagan** — group expense-splitting app para sa barkada/family trips. Yung classic na "sino nakabayad, magkano utang ko" problem na laging nangyayari pagkatapos ng trip, yun yung sinosolusyunan niya. Multiple payers per expense, net balance across groups, offline-first (kasi madalas walang signal sa beach/bundok), tapos settle up with proof of payment.

Simula palang to and I'm always open to suggestions and feedback — if there's a feature you'd love to see or anything that could be better, drop it in the comments. I'd genuinely love to hear from you. 🙏

Available now on iOS: [[https://apps.apple.com/app/ambagan-ph/id6779220285](https://apps.apple.com/app/ambagan-ph/id6779220285)](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fph%2Fapp%2Fambagan-ph%2Fid6779220285&h=AUAun33hkIZDELtOXqZOLf9W3STIB4gigRf3l_k0ftS_KhhXIrGY7E4BvtmHTZ1I26luovPT-EqdZ6-LgBYCmaOirhFt2cL9fu63TCdlJwr6y2bK751iu2exGo57aiRtuhbjuUENPILMNt1WSoj4mw&__tn__=-UK-R&c[0]=AUAlKh8xjmm1i9IyjpvUiRwGa1xHq2k2Qskx11bIq8xz9w2VhJ_dJt4v9omKOURGWRW1AZ9SXZREPl0rY2d-3zo_n8M9NxhegOWV4xhFxCvmwWC4ve48eu91UvhaqyxnGt9cwDNUlZEO77Ad87k-kBPUXEwaZe-87TJSCRlUvQ)

Finally submitted my app to App Builders PH!

**GWA Genie: Your Grade Wizard** 📚✨

A clean, fast, and privacy-friendly **GWA Calculator** built specifically for Filipino students.

✅ Calculate your General Weighted Average instantly
✅ Organize your subjects, units, and grades in one workspace
✅ View semester summaries, best/worst grades, and total units
✅ Get motivation based on your current academic standing 💙
✅ 100% private - your data stays in your browser and is never uploaded anywhere

I built this to provide students with a simple, distraction-free tool for tracking their academic progress without worrying about privacy.

I'd really appreciate your feedback, suggestions, or feature requests. Thank you to the App Builders PH community for inspiring indie developers like me to keep building! 🚀

text:
About a month ago, I shared the first version of TerraSentri here.

It all started with a simple thought after an earthquake:

**"Are my family and loved ones okay?"**

That question became the motivation behind building TerraSentri. Since then, I've been listening to feedback, iterating, and continuously improving the app. I wanted to share where the project is today.

# **What's new in TerraSentri?**
# 🌍 **Global earthquake monitoring**

TerraSentri is now **available internationally**. You can save and monitor important places anywhere in the world—whether it's your **parents in the Philippines, your sibling in Japan, your workplace in California**, or your own home overseas.

This also means **OFWs can monitor their loved ones back home** and receive personalized alerts whenever an earthquake affects their family's area.

⚙️ **Re-engineered backend**

The biggest changes weren't visible to users. Redesigning TerraSentri's event pipeline to efficiently process hazard data from multiple API/Data sources, deduplicate across providers, and fan out alerts to affected users without scaling costs linearly with user count. Along the way, optimizing the caching strategy, database indexing, and notification delivery path — keeping everything within the free tier while supporting fast alerting for a growing user base.

🔔 **Configurable earthquake alerts**

Not everyone wants the same notifications. Some people asked to be informed about every earthquake, while others preferred alerts only for stronger events to reduce anxiety of receiving notifications every now and then. You can now choose the minimum magnitude that triggers notifications.

🚨 **National-level alerts**

Magnitude **7.0 and above** earthquakes now trigger national-level notifications. **Users in the affected country **receive an alert, even if the earthquake isn't close to one of their saved locations, because events of that scale can have widespread impact.

👥 **Community updates**

I also created a Facebook community for anyone who wants to stay informed about earthquakes and follow TerraSentri's development, even if they don't have the app installed yet.

[[https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61590773997199](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61590773997199)](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61590773997199)

Building TerraSentri has been a great learning experience—from backend architecture and notification systems to product design and user feedback. There's still a long way to go, but I'm excited to keep improving it one iteration at a time.

As always, I'd love to hear your thoughts, feedback, or suggestions. Hopefully, I'll get to meet many of you at our **FIRST COMMUNITY MEET UP SOOOOOONNN**

text:
Hi everyone! 👋

I'd like to introduce **Vendora POS**, a project that our team has been working on with one goal in mind, to help small retail business owners digitalize their daily operations without the high cost and complexity of traditional POS systems.

We noticed that many small businesses still rely on notebooks, spreadsheets, or manual processes to manage their sales and inventory. As their business grows, these methods become harder to manage and often lead to inventory errors, inaccurate reports, and wasted time. That's why we built Vendora POS, a cloud based platform that brings sales, inventory, customers, reports, and payments into one simple and easy to use system.

What makes Vendora POS even better is that it comes with a built in **e commerce feature**. As soon as you publish your first product, you can instantly have your own online store and start accepting online orders. Your inventory stays synced between your physical store and online store, so you don't have to manage them separately.

The platform is designed for grocery stores, coffee shops, hardware stores, convenience stores, pharmacies, and other retail businesses that want an easier way to manage and grow their business. Our mission is to make digital tools accessible, even for small businesses that are just starting their journey.

The best part is that **Vendora POS is completely free to use for now** while we continue improving the platform based on feedback from business owners. As we add more features and continue to grow, we plan to introduce an affordable subscription model in the future. For now, we'd love for businesses to experience the platform and be part of its journey.

If you'd like to learn more or give it a try, you can visit our app page here:

👉 [https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/vendora-pos](https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/vendora-pos)

We'd really appreciate your feedback, suggestions, and support as we continue building Vendora POS. Thank you! ❤️

Milestone Hit: I'm officially sharing my first live project ever! 🎉

Meet Zen Berry—a personal productivity tool I built because I was tired of apps that didn't fit how I actually work.

As a solo developer, I've always struggled with:
- Rigid timers that don't match my rhythm
- Overwhelming task lists that never end
- Burning out trying to keep up with "productivity" expectations

So I built something that works for ME. And now I'm sharing it with YOU.

Zen Berry is simple, personal, and built for real people:
⏰ A timer you can set to ANY duration—minutes or hours
🎯 Just 3 Most Important Tasks—focus on what actually matters
🧠 A Brain Dump—capture everything, organize later
📌 Pins—quick notes for anything
📊 Analytics—see your progress without judgment
🤖 AI insights with agentic behavior—coming soon to help you find your rhythm and help you prioritizing your tasks and setting up your pace!

Is it perfect? Nope. 😅
I'm still working on the terms of use and privacy policy, so consider this a "soft launch" for early feedback.

But all the MVPs are implemented and tested. It works. And I'm proud of it.

If you've ever felt like productivity tools were working against you—I built this for you.

Final exam at Fudan: students don't answer questions. They write them — to stump AI.
51 students, 10 questions each, 3 AI models (Claude, DeepSeek, MiniMax) on the hot seat. The harder you make AI fail, the higher your grade.
Result? 50 students made at least one AI trip. Only 4 managed a perfect 0/10 against all models. Average score: 85.7.
"True understanding means finding AI's blind spots. That's not luck — it's skill." — Prof. XIAO Yanghua at College of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence.
From memorizing algorithms to outsmarting them. The classroom is evolving. 🧠⚡

text:
Just a morning question mga fellow app builder, paano po system nyo na mag market research at mag validate ng ideas nyo na it will sell or viral. And ano po full systematic plan nyo sa buong development process.

edit: ano rin po pala gamit nyo pang gawa ng slide deck sa apps nyo pangdisplay pic sa appstores.

topComments.text:
1. Validate your idea first with your friends or target users. Ask if they would actually use it. It’s even better if your idea comes from a problem you’ve personally experienced, because you’ll understand the pain point better.

2. Check the App Store to see if an app like yours already exists. Then build and ship as quickly as possible. Start with an MVP, just one simple feature that solves the core problem. Avoid adding complex features at the beginning. Focus on a specific niche. 
Then learn distribution sa fb, tiktok and threads. The game is 30% building, 70% marketing. Market fast, get feedback as many as possible.
If no one downloads or uses it, learn from the experience and move on. 

3. Use tools like ChatGPT, Claud Design or  Figma to speed up your design

I’m currently developing a tool that would simplify your customer validation. You may use it for concept validation or mvp testing, anything na need ng insighting. Instead of you giving out plain surveys or isa isang interview, you will be providing a link nalang to your users that initiates conversation with a chatbot. Siya na bahala maginterview sa respondents. Then, siya na din magconsolidate ng report for you. 

Im looking for pilot users sir, baka you’re planning to do some tests, pwede ko pagamit yung tool sayo. :)

text:
Prompt:

Review this as an architecture-level design review, as if you were
hired to reject this system before it reaches production.

Your job is NOT to be polite. Your job is to find weaknesses.

Context:
- Purpose: [ano ginagawa ng system]
- Scale: [users/TPS expected]
- Stage: [MVP / production / legacy modernization]
- Non-negotiables: [e.g. financial integrity, uptime, compliance]

For every issue:
- Why it is a problem
- Real-world consequences
- Severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low) — relative to the context above
- A better approach

Do not praise anything unless it genuinely deserves it.
Call out overengineering, underengineering, and junior-level
decisions explicitly and explain why.

Here is the system: [lagay mo system mo dito]

text:
Sharing the app I made, hopefully someone will be able to test it.

Dead Line is a mobile app that lets you write "vault messages" — personal letters to your loved ones that are only delivered if you stop checking in for an extended period of time.

Here's how it works:

- Daily check-in — You check in once a day (a simple tap). If you miss enough consecutive check-ins, the app assumes something has happened to you.

- Vault messages — You write messages (e.g., final words, account access info, document locations, sentimental notes) and assign recipients. The first message is free; unlimited messages, recipients, and custom deadlines require a subscription.

- Delivery deadline — Each message has a deadline (default 365 days). If you haven't checked in by then, the message is sent to your recipients via email.

- Premium features — Unlimited messages, multiple recipients per message, no character limit, and custom delivery deadlines (you can shorten or extend when each message sends).

- Secure — Messages are stored encrypted.

text:
Hello everyone!

I've been building Propello because proposals are one of those parts of client work that can quietly slow everything down. As someone who makes proposals on a daily basis, this has always been my pain-point in our company.

You already talked to the client. You already understand the project. But then you still need to turn messy notes, PDF briefs, scope decisions, pricing, timelines, terms, and requirements into something clear enough to send.

Propello is my attempt to make that workflow faster with AI. ⚡

It helps service teams move from brief to client-ready draft by combining:
* 🤖 AI proposal generation from briefs, RFPs, and internal notes
* 🧠 AI requirements assistant for clarifying what the client actually needs
* 🔗 Guided questionnaire and client invite links
* ✍️ Editable proposal preview before sending
* 📄 Branded PDF export
* 🧱 Templates, reusable scope blocks, and industry profiles
* 💸 Pricing packages, line items, milestones, and payment terms
* ✅ Review status, approval notes, and version snapshots
* 🗂️ Invoices, dashboard/history, quick search, and find-in-proposal
* 🤝 Sharing, real-time collaboration, and Supabase-backed accounts

The landing page is also coming together around the same promise: AI-assisted proposals for real service teams that need to scope, price, review, and ship client work faster. 🚀

Propello is still in beta testing, and I'm planning to launch it very soon. I would love feedback from builders, agencies, consultants, freelancers, and service teams here in App Builders PH.

Comment if you want beta access. 🙌

text:
Napansin ko lang 🤔ang dami nang web & mobile apps ngayon. From hobby apps to full SaaS. And honestly? Ang ganda ng mga output. Salamat sa AI, ang bilis na mag-ship ngayon.

Pero let me say the uncomfortable part: “Building & coding is no longer the moat.”

Kasi yung AI na nagpabilis sa'yo mag-build? Same tool na nagpabilis din sa lahat. The barrier didn't drop for you lang, bumaba siya para sa lahat, at the same time. So kung ang edge mo lang is "kaya kong mag-code ng app," congrats! kasama mo na ang milyong ibang tao.

The real bottleneck was never building. It's DISTRIBUTION.

Puno ang graveyard ng magagandang app na walang user. Technically solid, ganda ng UI, pero walang nakakaalam na existing. Kasi ang building, yan yung masarap na part 🙂 yung ego, yung dopamine ng "gumagana na!" Ang distribution naman? Boring. Mahirap. Paulit-ulit. Kaya nga yun ang MOAT ngayon kasi karamihan ayaw gawin.

At hindi lang basta "i-market mo" ha. Ibig sabihin may hawak kang problema na alam mo nang husto yung depth na di kayang i-replicate ng AI kasi walang context. TRUST. Yung mga tao na maghihintay sa susunod mong ilalabas.

Ang mga devs na mananalo sa susunod na taon hindi yung pinakamagaling mag-code. Coding is becoming table stakes. Panalo yung nakakaintindi ng tao, ng market, ng isang specific na problema na kaya nilang solusyunan nang mas malalim kaysa kahit sino.

So keep building guys. Seriously 💪 wag kang titigil. Pero fall in love sa problema at sa user, hindi sa code. Yung code, commodity na yan. Yung understanding kung sinong tinutulungan mo at bakit sila magbabayad , yun ang hindi.

Building is the entry fee na ngayon. Hindi na yun ang prize.

text:
**Hey App Builders PH! **

**Sharing something I've been building.**

**Furry Places** — a pet-friendly establishment finder with geospatial search, built to help pet owners actually find places (cafés, restaurants, hotels, parks, etc.) that welcome their animals, instead of guessing or scrolling through outdated Facebook comments.

**What it does:**
🗺️ Discover pet-friendly spots near you with live map + list search, filters (type, verified, distance radius), and sorting by nearest/top-rated/popular
🐕 Missing pet reports - post a lost pet, get matched with sightings in the area
📅 Community pet events - find and register for local meetups, adoption drives, etc.
🏠 Shelter directory
🛍️ A (rolling out) pet marketplace for vendors/products
⭐ Reviews & photos with a full moderation queue, so listings stay trustworthy
🔔 Email + web push notifications for nearby new places, event reminders, missing-pet alerts

**How it's built** (for the tech-curious):
* Bun monorepo, five packages: React Native/Expo mobile app, two Astro + React web apps (consumer + admin dashboard), a Cloudflare Workers API (Hono + tRPC + Drizzle), and a shared package
* PostGIS geometry columns for real geospatial queries (radius search, nearest-first sorting)
* Better Auth for auth (email/password, Google OAuth, mobile bearer tokens)
* CockroachDB in production via Cloudflare Hyperdrive

Visit it at: https://furry-places.periabyte.dev/

text:
BIR compliance notes for software sellers. SPM vs POS, accreditation, and PTU requirements. 

Sharing this for anyone navigating the same questions. 

Beginner dev here. Sharing my BIR notes. Let me know if I missed anything. 

What are your thoughts? 

---

❝ Under BIR regulations, any machine or software used for business operations, even for inventory tracking, generally needs to be registered with the BIR and have a Permit to Use (PTU). The rules are designed to ensure the BIR can effectively monitor business activities, and they make a clear distinction based on what the machine does.

---

topComments.text: I've experienced the process of accrediting a POS with BIR and the process is far from optimal. Para kang nag thethesis tas yung mga panels mo iba iba gusto and there's no "one" standard. It took us 1 and a half year bago ma-accredit ang POS namin. What a waste of time.
I was taken aback by this. If it says, any machine, what if a personal device interfaces with the BIR-registered application, like a tablet? This needs to be registered, too?

topComments.text:
Idea is nice, try to improve the UI, you can ask claude to create design systems, audit contrasts, visual hierarchy. 

It’s a good start, just continue improving the UI and UX.

Just like your short term rentals. Register it in BIR, DTI or SEC and have your Business Permit. Those are the basics.

Hire a proper developer, cybersecurity, database engineer and cloud team for starters to comply with Data Privacy Act of 2012.

Hire accountants to support and advice you on your app’s accounting processes.

It’s better to be on the safe side than have costly legal complaints later on.

AI is just a tool to help people build their MVP. You still need a full team to deploy it SAFELY and maintain the SECURITY of your users.

BIR will also consider your app as POS/CAS if it is publicly available.

topComments.text:
Congrats sa pag-viral, pero grabe nga ang heart attack sa bill! 😅

Ibig sabihin niyan, may malaking asset (tulad ng mabigat na image, video, o code bundle) na paulit-ulit na dina-download ng mga users kasi hindi naka-cache nang maayos.
Ipagawa mo agad ito sa Developer mo ngayon din:

1. Ilagay sa likod ng Cloudflare (Free Tier): Ito ang pinakamabilis na salbabida. Si Cloudflare na ang sasalo sa bandwidth/traffic nang libre, kaya hindi na tatama ang bill kay Firebase.

2. Ayusin ang Cache-Control Headers: Siguraduhing naka-set sa ⁠firebase.json⁠ na i-cache ng browser ang mga static assets para iisang beses lang ida-download ng user.
￼

3. Check for Infinite Loops: I-inspect ang network tab baka may code na paulit-ulit na nagre-request ng files kada segundo nang hindi niyo namamalayan.

Pm moko pd ko check, pero need ntn ng access sa code, firebase, at cloud console mo. 

Kaya pa i-salba yan para sa susunod na araw, barya na lang ang babayaran mo!
we can't help if you don't know the problem lol

**It's been a month since I launched the **[VA Workers PH](https://www.facebook.com/groups/980298767865372/user/100064292971071/?__cft__[0]=AZaX0YRjS5aBHDsAXrX00gsVy0cjbh7LWPa73qoyhX1ZRSOChrOHEC1osEiIw9evBp4_uDGlhpdPYFe5-GDzWe6xFN2j-CSzp2gBOSxQ6XLhZoMRfX7Q374-d-65ZvhjOiesoHjGKAyuHyIFKOWCFY8S&__tn__=-]K-R)** job board **and I want to thank everyone for their help in getting the word out for the site and making it better through feedback**.**

**Some stats for the site since launch:**
**Current Community**
* **17,700+** Registered Users

**Last 30 Days (Traffic & Engagement)**
* **52,000** Monthly Active Users
* **149,000** Total Visits
* **405,000** Page Views

**Biggest Achievement: People are getting hired through the site and they are advocating for it on their own.**

**Very thankful because they both motivate me to do better and they give social proof that the site is legit and helpful.**

The site is doing better than I ever expected metrics-wise so there's been lessons and challenges associated with that growth.

**Lessons**:

1. Beef up security before launch. Thankful for the white hats for the warnings and recommendations.
2. Adjust the site when everyone's asleep lol. Something breaking at 5:30 AM is better than 1:00 PM.
3. Test, test, test, and test some more. Make sure anything you add works as intended.
4. Be open to recommendations. A lot of UX improvements since launch came from users.

**Challenges**:
1. Unexpected expenses due to hitting account limits. There's a ton of people using the site and I want to give them a smooth experience so I pay out of pocket lol.

2. Be clear what the website/app does. It isn't clear to some people that the site aggregates jobs from the VA Workers PH group (though it's indicated in the FAQs on the home page) and they think I'm handling applications myself.

3. Proving legitimacy. Hard to build trust when scam job postings are everywhere. But I've been running this community for two years, the site is free, and I'm the one covering the costs. Thankful for everyone who's spoken up and vouched for it.

Anyway, I plan on launching a SaaS site that complements VAWorkersPH perfectly soon and I hope you support that as well. 

We're also open for ads and collaborations. :)

Took a look at the current AppBuildersPH directory today.

We’re now at:
• 237 apps
• 198 users
• 932 upvotes

A few interesting things stood out.

The biggest categories are Productivity, Business, Education, Finance, and Lifestyle.

Finance has the most upvotes, while AI has the highest engagement per app despite having fewer listings.

What I like most is that this isn’t driven by a handful of people. Most makers have only one app listed, which means more builders are shipping and sharing their work.

One thing I’d love to improve is feedback. People are upvoting apps, but not leaving many comments. I think builders would benefit a lot from more suggestions, bug reports, and product feedback from the community.

text:
Right now, anyone can use AI to generate an entire application over a weekend. It feels like magic. But behind the sleek UI of these rapid-fire apps is a massive hidden risk: the code looks clean, but it’s often structurally hollow against attacks.
Right now, anyone can use AI to generate an entire application over a weekend. It feels like magic. But behind the sleek UI of these rapid-fire apps is a massive hidden risk: the code looks clean, but it’s often structurally hollow against attacks.

​AI models are trained to write code that functions, not code that resists exploitation. They routinely copy legacy patterns, miss input validation, and introduce classic vulnerabilities like SQL injection and XSS.

​If developers trust AI blindly and ship straight to production without rigorous security testing—skipping automated scans, proxy traffic analysis, and dependency checks—they aren't just launch-ready. They are breached-ready.

​The Bottom Line:

AI is a powerful co-pilot, but it is not a certified security auditor. Velocity means absolutely nothing if you are delivering a product that compromises user data on day one.

​We need to stop treating security testing as an afterthought or a bottleneck. In the AI era, a robust testing pipeline isn’t a luxury—it’s the only thing standing between a successful launch and a catastrophic liability. 🔒

​#CyberSecurity #AppDevelopment #AI #DataPrivacy #ApplicationSecurity

Hi everyone! Share ko lang yung personal project ko na currently ginagawa ko, called LibriQ.

LibriQ is a book-tracking web app built with HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript. It lets users search books, add them to a personal library, track reading progress, rate books, favorite books, view book details, refresh missing metadata, and check reading statistics.

It uses Open Library and Google Books for book data, tapos "localStorage" muna for saving the user’s library.

Current features:

- Book search using Open Library + Google Books

- Personal library with reading status filters

- Reading progress tracking

- Star ratings

- “About this book” section

- Metadata refresh

- Dashboard and statistics

- Responsive UI for desktop and mobile

Still in development pa siya, so I’d really appreciate feedback sa UI, features, or anything na pwedeng ma-improve.

Live demo: https://libriq.vercel.app/

Thank you!

Hello po 2nd year Web Development student, I want to share what I have build.

While researching challenges in education, I learned that many educators in the Philippines still struggle to find modern teaching tools and educational resources in one accessible place. Resources are often scattered across different websites, making them harder to discover and adopt.

That inspired me to build Sinammon, an open-source platform that aims to serve as a centralized hub for teaching tools, educational resources, AI Tools all in one organized place. This project has challenged me to think beyond writing code and focus on building something that could create real value for others. I'm still improving it, and I'd love to hear your feedback, suggestions, or ideas for features that could make it more useful.
