text:
** 📢 Community Update: Anonymous Posting & Commenting**

Good evening App Builders!

The mod team has been deliberating on this since June, and after weighing the pros and cons, we've decided to disable anonymous posting and commenting in the group starting now.

A few reasons behind this:

**We've grown a lot.** What used to be a small group has scaled significantly, and with that growth comes way more activity for the mod team to review. 

Anonymous posts and comments take longer to moderate properly, and we want to spend that time actually supporting the community instead of being on the hunt for the next comment to flag.

**Accountability matters. **We built this group to be a space where builders can be real with each other — sharing wins, failures, hot takes, and honest feedback. 

Anon accounts make it easier for people to say things they wouldn't stand behind under their own name, and that's not the culture we want here.

I hope this does not come across as restrictive and more so come across about protecting the safe space and building more trust. 

Most of you already post under your real names and profiles, and that's exactly the kind of transparency that makes this group valuable. We just want that to be the standard for everyone.

Thanks for understanding, and as always, feel free to drop questions or concerns in the comments (yes, with your name on it ).

— App Builders PH Mod Team 

@everyone

text:
Magandang araw!

Sharing lang yung ginagawa kong app called BatasPH.ai

Kapag nating malaman kung ano talaga ang sinasabi ng batas, ang una nating ginagawa ay i-type ito sa Google. Madalas ay mga blog post, forum thread, SEO content farm, kahit mga Facebook post, magkakahalo, may paminsan-minsang opisyal na resource. Kapag dumirekta naman sa opisyal na site ay malalalim na pananalitang ingles ang mga makikita. Mas lalong nahihirapan kapag Tagalog ang tanong, dahil mas kakaunti ang resulta at kadalasang natatabunan ang mga tama at opisyal na documento.

Ang BatasPH.ai ai isang libreng serbisyo para sa mga ganitong pagkakataon. Itanong mo ang iyong katanungan sa Filipino o English, at automatic na ie-extract ng app ang mga legal na termino at konseptong nakapaloob dito, at ginagamit ang mga ito kasama ng orihinal mong tanong para maghanap sa mga lehitimong mga resources: tulad ng opisyal na mga website ng gobyerno ng Pilipinas at kinikilalang mga legal repository, hindi kailanman mga blog o social media.

Makukuha mo ang aktwal na teksto ng batas, kaagapay ng mga citations na kaya mong i-verify sa sarili mo, at isang paliwanag sa simpleng wika na madali mong maiintindihan.

---

May mga tinatapos na lang ako ng mga tests, at sinusubukang magtabi ng pondo para sa gagawin kong closed beta. Claude API ang gamit ko since dito ako certified at may mga approaches na naka embed na tulad ng request caching, etc., na makakatulong sa pagpapababa ng token usage.

Sa ngayong ay up na ang app ang site at na register ko na rin sa website ni App Builders PH: https://www.appbuildersph.com/apps/batasph-ai

Pero sa ngayon ay privacy, roadmap at whitepaper pa lang ang accessible.

Thank you!

Pickleball has officially taken over my life. 😂

One thing my friends and I kept complaining about was how hard it was to find available courts.

Every venue seems to use a different booking platform, so whenever we wanted to play we'd end up opening multiple websites just to answer one question:

*"May available ba this weekend?"*

After getting tired of doing that over and over again, we decided to build something for it. They gave me the idea to build 𝘱𝘪𝘤𝘬𝘥.

𝘱𝘪𝘤𝘬𝘥. makes it easier to find a court without the usual chaos. 

In one place, you can:

• Search available courts by date and time

• Filter by district, surface type, and price

• Compare venues side by side

• See hourly availability at a glance

• Jump straight to booking when you find a slot

The goal is simple:

Spend less time searching and more time actually playing.

text:
Lumitrail - Augmented Reality Sketchpad (Personal Project)
Honestly, bigla lang talaga akong nagka-idea tapos tinuloy ko with the help of Claude AI.

Napaisip lang ako, what if pwede kang mag-drawing virtually tapos yung lines mag-stay talaga sa paligid mo? Parang mga metaverse demos, pero walang headset, walang app na ida-download, walang setup. Open mo lang yung link tapos gamitin mo.

Simple lang siya. Open mo sa Chrome sa Android phone mo, hold the screen, then move your phone around. Pwede mo pa siyang lakaran at nandun pa rin siya exactly where you drew it.

Ang ginawa ko na challenge is Walang server na nagpo-process, walang database, wala. Lahat ginagawa mismo ng phone mo inside the browser.

Na-test ko pa ito sa luma kong Huawei P30 Pro. Hindi flagship, hindi latest phone. Chrome lang gamit ko.

Hindi rin naman ako software developer by title. Mahilig lang talaga akong gumawa ng kung anu-anong ideas at i-figure out kung paano sila gagana. Malaking tulong si Claude sa coding, pero yung concept at direction, gusto ko lang talagang makita kung posible.

Built with Three.js, WebXR, and Vercel. Runs directly on your phone, no install needed.

text:
I've always wanted to build an application where we can connect our own thoughts from different books from different authors and maaaan this is a god send. We are currently trying out how the graph works and how it feels, so if you're interested do let us know if you like it or not, there's a free promo code on the website so you can test it out for free.

Just a brief overview of what ZenRead is before you test it:

**Essence of ZenRead:**

Imagine reading a line by Marcus Aurelius about resilience. Two years later, you read a modern psychology paper on grit. In every other app, those two thoughts die alone in their respective books. In ZenRead, you draw a line between them.

**The Mechanics of Insight:**
* Capture**: **Point your camera at a page. OCR grabs the text. No typing. No friction.
* Link: See a connection? Drag a thread from this quote to that one. 
* Visualize: Watch your library transform from a flat list into a living, breathing constellation of ideas.

This isn't a book tracker. It's an external cortex for your physical library and It turns passive consumption into active synthesis. **While everyone else is busy rating books to impress strangers**, you are quietly weaving a tapestry of wisdom that actually makes you smarter. 

**Don't just read. Evolve.**

Website: [https://zenread.pro/](https://zenread.pro/)

Playstore: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=pro.zenread.app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=pro.zenread.app)

We're still iterating over our application so do report some bugs if you come across any.

text:
**Just because you can build it doesn’t mean you should.**

One thing I hope we continue to build in AppBuildersPH is not just technical excellence, but responsibility.

Recently, I’ve seen projects shared that involve piracy, bypassing paid services, or other tools designed to skirt laws or someone else’s work. While they may be technically impressive, they’re not the kind of projects we want to celebrate here.

Let’s build products that we’re proud to ship. Not just because they’re possible, but because they’re responsible.

**Build responsibly.**

topComments.text: What does piracy or skirting someone else’s work mean here actually? Because to me unless you patented the concept it doesn’t mean that other people cannot build same idea as yours. At the end of the day everything is about giving the best and secured user experience

This is exactly the conversation we need to have right now. Thank you for bringing this up, Bryl.

The democratization of development through vibe-coding has been a double-edged sword. On one hand, it lowers the barrier to entry. On the other hand, it has created a culture where people build and sell systems they have absolutely no experience managing or securing, heavily relying on unstable AI code.

We are seeing a flood of 'vibe-coded' applications (like POS systems, TNVS, etc.) being distributed or sold without any of the necessary legal permits or tax compliances processed beforehand. When these unstable systems inevitably break, the builders ghost their clients.

This is from my experience. I have clients who used vibe-coded systems and was left for dead by the vibe-coders after being fully paid.

There is a massive difference between building a fun side project and shipping a product that impacts someone's business or data. I don't condemn vibe-coding for exploration, but I strongly condemn the lack of accountability from those building purely for clout or quick profit.

Technical excellence means nothing without a sense of stewardship for what we put out into the world.

text:
Hello Builders👋

Built something a bit different from the usual mobile/web projects — an open-source cybersecurity toolkit called **Viper**.

*we bite.*

Viper is a precision recon & security toolkit focused on **signal over noise**.

Instead of dumping noisy outputs like traditional tools, I wanted something that feels clean, fast, and intentional — almost like a product-first security tool.

Core ideas:
• Fast by default (latency-aware scans)
• Clean CLI UX
• Recon-first workflow
• Scan history + diff tracking
• HTML + JSON reports

Some commands:
* `viper bite target.com` → fast recon
* `viper venom target.com` → full scan
* `viper diff target.com` → compare scans over time

Built with:
* Python
* Click
* Rich
* Docker support

What I enjoyed most building this wasn’t just functionality—it was designing the product philosophy, command structure, architecture, and UX.

Trying to make even a terminal tool feel polished and premium.

Open source + MIT licensed.

Would love thoughts from fellow builders 👀
Especially around product design, architecture, or branding.

Github Repo: [https://github.com/Carlwyne-Dev/viper](https://github.com/Carlwyne-Dev/viper)

text:
Hi everyone!

I'm a 2nd-year BSIT student, and I'd like to share a project I've been working on called AnoUlam.

The idea came from a simple problem that I often noticed at home: many filipinos sometimes have ingredients available but don't know what dish they can cook with them. Instead of searching manually every time, I thought it would be interesting to build an application that could recommend Filipino dishes based on ingredients entered by the user. The app's target user is Filipinos. 

I challenged myself to build the solution even if I feel like I can't do it

Through this project, I gained hands-on experience with:

• React Native (Expo)

• Spring Boot

• MySQL

• REST APIs

• Docker

• Cloud Deployment

• Database Hosting

• Mobile Application Development

The application allows users to search ingredients they already have and receive matching dish recommendations.

As a student developer, this project challenged me in many areas, especially debugging, deployment, cloud hosting, mobile development, and connecting frontend, backend, and database systems together.

I'm sharing it here to gather feedback from developers and real users. Any suggestions, advice, bug reports, or recommendations for improvement would be greatly appreciated.

APK Download:

https://expo.dev/accounts/dev_jude12/projects/AnoUlam/builds/c37ee498-843b-4e23-9e1c-6085fa4c2ebd

GitHub Repository:

https://github.com/jude342/anoulam-frontend

https://github.com/jude342/anoulam-backend

Thank you for taking the time to check it out. I'm still learning and would appreciate any feedback from the community!

text:
Hi mga bossing!

Sharing my vibe-coded web app for my personal 3D printing business.

I'm currently running a hybrid setup with a self-hosted backend, while the frontend is deployed entirely on free-tier services.

Kung nakita ninyo yung post ko about my homelab, isa ito sa mga services na naka-host dito sa bahay.

**Disclaimer:** I'm not a professional developer. I just found AI really interesting, and it's been a fun way to build something from an idea into a working application.

**Current Features**

- Offline/Online POS for our pop-up markets and bazaar events
- Product catalog with online ordering
- STL page where users can generate their own designs using parametric models

**Magkano ang nagastos para maging live ito?**

- Domain name: **$12.99/year**
- Electricity for my homelab: **around 30–50 AED/month (₱800)**

That's it.

**Everything else is running on free-tier services:**
* GitHub Actions for CI/CD
* Vercel for the frontend
* Brevo for email notifications
* Google Analytics for analytics
* Cloudflare for DNS, WAF, and DDoS protection

**Backend Infrastructure**

I currently have **6 nodes** working together, handling production, staging, monitoring, networking, and storage.

**- Node 1** – pfSense firewall + VLAN management
**- Node 2** – TrueNAS storage (3TB+ usable with automated backups)
**- Node 3** – Production backend
**- Node 4** – Production mirror (failover in case a node fails)
**- Node 5** – Staging + monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Uptime Kuma)
**- Node 6** – Networking services (Pi-hole, Nginx Proxy Manager)

**Total Resources**
* 6 nodes
* 168GB RAM
* 3TB SSD
* 16TB archive storage

I also designed a zero-trust network using pfSense with four isolated VLANs:

**- VLAN 10** – Management (trusted admin zone)
**- VLAN 20** – Servers (application nodes, TrueNAS, Docker)
**- VLAN 30** – Home network (trusted personal devices)
**- VLAN 40** – DMZ (internet-facing services only)

**Cloud Cost Comparison**

Considering the total compute resources I already have, I've saved a significant amount by self-hosting.

A rough comparison, based on equivalent compute, RAM, storage, and redundancy, not just the backend application would look something like this:

* **My homelab:** $13/month electricity
* **AWS equivalent:** $800–1,000/month
* **Azure equivalent:** $900–1,100/month

Of course, cloud infrastructure has its own advantages. You get managed services, higher availability, and a lot more peace of mind.

Self-hosting comes with trade-offs. You need to think about power outages, internet reliability, cooling, backups, hardware maintenance, and disaster recovery. I wouldn't recommend it for every project, especially high-traffic production systems.

For me, the biggest value has been the learning experience.

AI has made it much easier to turn ideas into working software, even for someone without a traditional software development background.

If you've been thinking about building something, don't let the cost stop you. There are so many generous free tiers available today. Start small, keep learning, and build little by little.

📱🔧 Got a broken TV or AC remote? Don't throw it away just yet!

If you have another working remote to copy from—or even a phone with an IR blaster—you might not need to buy a replacement anymore.

Since I have an Electronics Engineering background, I've always been fascinated by infrared communication and remote control technology. That curiosity inspired me to create RemoteControl Cloner, an open-source app for cloning and managing IR remote signals.

🚧 The project is still in its testing phase, so I'd really appreciate your feedback, bug reports, and suggestions to help improve it.

If you're into electronics, embedded systems, or just enjoy building cool projects, feel free to check it out!

🔗 GitHub Repository:

https://github.com/engrpanda/RemoteControl_Cloner 

If you like the project, a ⭐ on GitHub would really help!

And one last thing... please don't "test" it on your neighbor's TV or the TVs at the mall. 🤣📺

Hey everyone,

I'm looking for beta testers for a new personal finance app I'm developing called BudgetRaker. If you're looking to get a better handle on your finances, track your net worth, or just want a clean way to log your expenses, I'd love for you to try it out!

 Features:

Comprehensive Tracking: Easily track your accounts, daily transactions, and monitor your overall Net Worth over time.

Smart Organization: Manage your recurring transactions, set up bill reminders, and track active debts all in one place.

Savings Goals: Set custom savings goals and watch your progress grow as you save.

Built-in Calculator: A handy inline calculator keypad so you can do quick math right while you log transactions.

AI Coach Insights: Get smart, AI-driven insights and suggestions based on your spending habits to help you save more effectively.

 How to join the test:

Join our Google Group to get access to the beta track: [https://groups.google.com/g/budgetraker](https://groups.google.com/g/budgetraker?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTAAYnJpZBExRndjV2JNS1JWYWVxQ2ZvZHNydGMGYXBwX2lkEDIyMjAzOTE3ODgyMDA4OTIAAR5pWCEYOLk4yeG1VuYk1OdLVGhcNbu7BhE3T6d-5cDrqZaEtul-NMVhpVrXKQ_aem_73of2HKIhWawKS5A5dPwpw)

Hey everyone! 👋 As someone who loves our beautiful province, I’ve been working on a passion project: a mobile tourism app dedicated entirely to Romblon!

The goal is to make traveling around our islands seamless for both locals and tourists. While the app is still a work in progress and not fully functional yet, I’ve already built some pretty cool features:

🗺️ AI Trip Generator – Instantly map out your itinerary.

💬 Chat Support – Quick assistance for travelers on the go.

📍 Travel Footprints & Memories – Track where you’ve been and look back at your favorite moments.

🚢 Ferry Schedules & Port Info – No more guessing boat departures!

Right now, I have over 200+ amazing places mapped out, but I’m still improving the database and I want to make sure every hidden gem is included.

This is where I need your help! 🙏

If you are a local, a frequent traveler, or a photographer who loves capturing Romblon, I would love to collaborate with you! I’m looking for:

Hidden Gems: Spots, beaches, or local eateries that aren't on the usual tourist maps yet.

Photos: High-quality shots of places around Romblon that you'd be willing to let me feature in the app (with full credit to you, of course! 📸).

Let’s showcase the true beauty of Romblon to the world together. If you have photos to share or want to suggest a spot, drop a comment below or send me a DM!

Thank you so much! 🌊🥥

#Romblon #TravelRomblon #DiscoverRomblon #AppDevelopment #BuildInPublic #PhilippineTourism

text:
Nakakatuwa lang isipin na dati, pangarap ko lang gumawa ng sarili kong system o app... pero ngayon, ginagamit na talaga namin sa actual business namin. ❤️

Proud akong i-share na nakagawa ako ng sarili naming Web App para sa maliit naming business na "SwiunFix Computer Repair Services", at ang mas nakakatuwa, ginawa ko ito through the power of vibe coding and AI tools. 🤖💻

Meron na kaming:

✅ Repair Tracking

✅ Online Booking

✅ Customer Dashboard

✅ Cost Estimator

✅ AI Assistant

✅ Reviews

✅ Payment Portal

at marami pang iba!

Parang dati, pang malaking kumpanya lang yung ganitong system. Ngayon, meron na rin ang maliit naming computer repair shop. 🙌

Ang totoo niyan, matagal ko nang passion ang system at app building. Gustong-gusto ko talaga ang coding at paggawa ng mga bagay na nakakatulong sa tao at negosyo.

Pero hindi ko siya na-pursue noon dahil sa realidad ng buhay.

Wala kaming sapat na kakayahan noon para makabili ng laptop o magkaroon ng sariling PC para makapag-aral at makapag-practice ng programming. Kasi simple lang ang buhay namin at kailangan unahin ang mas importanteng pangangailangan.

Kaya siguro sobrang fulfilling para sa akin na makita na ngayon, nakakagawa na ako ng mga bagay na dati hanggang pangarap lang.

Nakakatuwa rin isipin na minsan hindi pala kailangan dumaan sa traditional na paraan para makagawa ng isang bagay. Minsan kailangan mo lang ng curiosity, tiyaga, willingness matuto, at tamang tools para makapagsimula.

Hindi man ako naging traditional programmer, pero nakakatuwang makita na nakakagawa pa rin ako ng mga system na may totoong gamit sa totoong negosyo.

"Small wins matter", ika nga❤️

Excited ako sa mga susunod pang maidaragdag sa system at kung paano pa nito mapapaganda ang experience ng aming customers sa SwiunFix.

Sa mga may pangarap din na gumawa ng sarili nilang app, system, o business tool , baka mas malapit na kayo kaysa sa iniisip ninyo.

text:
Hi everyone

I made a karaoke queueing web app: KaraoQueue https://www.karaoqueue.live/

This started as a personal-use project when I hang out with friends. We tried existing queuing apps like karadeo.com, mykaraoke.party, etc. but ran into the same issue, some videos wouldn't play because embed is disabled.

I also tried existing chrome extensions like YouTube Karaoke Extension and MyYouTubeKaraoke. But with those, only the person with the extension can queue songs, not other devices.

So I made an app that combines both. It uses a chrome extension as the player (so videos play directly on youtube, no embed issues), while still letting everyone queue songs from their own phones.

Feel free to use the app and let me know if you have any feedback!

For more details check the website:
app: https://www.karaoqueue.live/
extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/lhkggahjdljmnhddmhbiclaaabonhbab

Hi everyone! 👋 I’m excited to share a personal project I’ve been working on over the past few weeks: Musiciana 🎤✨

We all know how annoying it is during karaoke nights when you have to wait for a song to completely finish just so you can search and type the next one. 🤦‍♂️ On top of that, dealing with constant ad interruptions completely ruins the vibe. 🛑

I built Musiciana to solve this: anyone can browse and queue up songs simultaneously while someone is singing, completely ad-free! 🎶

Here are the core features:

🔒 Secure Access: Quick and easy login using your Google accounts.

👥 Create & Join Rooms: Easily host a room or let friends join instantly via a QR code or room code.

🎵 Smart Queuing: Browse and line up songs on the fly without interrupting the current singer.

👑 Host Control: The host keeps total control over the room for a smooth, organized experience.

🚫 Ad-Free Jamming: Pure, uninterrupted music from start to finish.

⚠️ Quick Note on Compatibility:
As of now, I’ve only fully tested this on Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge on desktop/android. 🌐 It hasn’t been tested yet on other browsers or iOS (Safari/iPhone), so if you're using those, please expect that things might look or act a bit experimental! 📱💻

The platform is currently in its testing phase 🚀, and I would love to get your help. Please try it out, host a room with your friends, and feel free to drop any feedback—whether it's good or bad! 💬👇

text:
# **The "Vibe Coding" Boom is Here... But Are We Building Time Bombs?** 💣

Let’s be real, generative AI has completely changed the game for app builders. We’re shipping features faster than ever, spinning up entire applications through "vibe coding," and watching ideas come to life in minutes. It’s an incredible time to be a creator.

But while we’re riding the high of rapid deployment, a quiet crisis is brewing.

When AI generates code, it prioritizes *functionality* over *security*. It doesn't inherently understand your specific threat model. Right now, thousands of AI-assisted apps are being deployed with hidden vulnerabilities, misconfigured permissions, weak validation, and exposed endpoints. We are essentially building on top of ticking time bombs.

As builders, we can't let speed compromise integrity.

That’s exactly why I developed **GESF: Green Engineering Standard Framework.**

**GESF** is designed to act as the missing guardrail for your development workflow. It doesn’t just blindly scan; it intelligently guides you through your architecture, points out exactly where the critical security gaps are, and, crucially, **helps you fix them.**

**Specially built for long-term accountability, GESF has a Governance Provenance Chain.**

Instead of chasing scattered approval fragments across Jira, emails, and spreadsheets when auditors ask for proof, the `ges governance` command links 9 critical dimensions of system approval (from identity and risk assessment to evidence and review cycles) into a single defensible chain.

With just one command (`ges governance verify <id>`), you can instantly prove to auditors, examiners, and stakeholders exactly who approved the system, under what authority, and with what supporting evidence.

Whether you are fully vibe coding or blending AI generation with manual architecture, **GESF **ensures that what you build stays secure, compliant, and completely audit-ready without dragging down your momentum.

Check out the repository, star it, and let's start building faster and safer: 👉[[https://github.com/greenarmor/gesf](https://github.com/greenarmor/gesf)](https://github.com/greenarmor/gesf)

How are you handling security checks and compliance in your current AI workflows? Let’s discuss below! 👇

#AppBuilding #VibeCoding #GenerativeAI #Cybersecurity #OpenSource #GESF #GreenEngineering #TechGovernance

Hi everyone! Share ko lang yung personal project ko na currently ginagawa ko, called LibriQ.

LibriQ is a book-tracking web app built with HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript. It lets users search books, add them to a personal library, track reading progress, rate books, favorite books, view book details, refresh missing metadata, and check reading statistics.

- Responsive UI for desktop and mobile

* **Destinations** down to city level, **charters** with booking leads, species guide, events

* PWA-installable, SEO-ready, mobile-first.

text:
OFFICIAL RECOGNITION
Hello, esteemed builders. I was contemplating a suggestion: what if we were to formally register this group or organization with the SEC and appoint officials, such as a president? This would enable the group, under the name Appbuildersph, to conduct community outreach initiatives in the future. Such a formal structure would also facilitate easier negotiation and processing of necessary documents for collaborations with government agencies, for instance, when organizing seminars and training sessions, as the group would be officially recognized and registered. I am uncertain if all members would be amenable to contributing to the registration fees, but this would pave the way for Appbuilders to organize seminars, outreach programs, and even international participation with nominated members in the future.

topComments.text: I support the idea of SEC registration. Along with that, I hope we also adopt a code of ethics. As an official organization, we should not accept or assist projects involving piracy or any illegal content. That will help build the credibility and professionalism of our community.

I also support the idea of formally organizing and registering the group, as it can provide credibility and open more opportunities for collaborations, events, and community initiatives in the future.

That said, I believe it may not be necessary for the organization to be closely tied to government agencies. AppbuildersPH can remain an independent private organization while still hosting seminars, training programs, and other events. Partnerships with government institutions can always be explored when beneficial, but maintaining independence may provide greater flexibility in decision-making and operations.

This is simply my perspective, particularly considering the administrative and financial considerations that often come with government-related engagements. Nonetheless, I appreciate the discussion and the vision of helping the community grow through AppbuildersPH.

text:
Building an Impact-driven App
Hi everyone!

I built an app out of the hardest 17 years of my life.

I ended a long term relationship almost 4 months ago. 

Instead of letting the lessons, the pain, and the hope just become a memory, I turned them into a product.

It's called Tahanan OS. An AI powered family communication web app, built on Next.js, Firebase, and the Anthropic Claude API. 

The core feature is called the Buffer, an AI coach that helps you process and reframe a message before you send it in a heated moment.

I built it first for myself. It helped me heal. I still use it today.

Right now it's a web app, accessible on any browser, mobile or desktop. 

Converting it to a native iOS and Android app is on the roadmap, something I'm looking forward to learning and tackling next.

My hope is that this app outlives me...

That my kids, and their kids someday, won't have to figure out relationships the hard way or stay stuck in painful dynamics because nobody gave them a better system.

If that happens, I can see myself on my deathbed smiling. 😌

Sharing it here because I'd love feedback from fellow builders. 

What did I get right? What would you do differently?

Check it out: https://tahananos.com

P.S. If you know anyone in your family or circle who could use this, I'd really appreciate a mention or a share. No advertising budget yet, just trying to get it to the people who need it most.
previewTitle: Tahanan OS — Your AI Coach for Emotional Growth
previewDescription: A private space for Filipino families to process emotions, understand patterns, and choose their next words on purpose — before sending them. Less conflict. More connection.

When the light goes red, there's no room for a spinner.

That's why I built **CueCart** — a broadcast cartwall where every cue is loaded, ready, and waiting before you need it. You press a pad, and the sound is just *there*. Under 6ms. No spin-up, no lag, no dropouts — even when the show is busy and the room is loud.

It's got everything you need on one wall:

🎚️ A grid of pads you fire by touch or keyboard
🎧 A real DJ deck — jog, scratch, tempo, and headphone cue, without leaving the app
🎙️ Broadcast processing on every pad (compressor, limiter, presets)
📂 Drag-and-drop library that doesn't care where files live on disk
⚡ Instant, gapless bank and set switching for a whole show

And it's yours for life — one-time licence, no subscription treadmill.

Made for radio, live production, theatre, houses of worship, and podcast/streaming.

text:
**Introducing GuarDan** — a child monitoring and parental control application designed to help parents protect and guide their children in today's digital world.

As children spend more time online, parents face increasing challenges in keeping them safe from harmful content, excessive screen time, and online risks. GuarDan was built to provide parents with better visibility into their child's device activity while encouraging responsible digital habits.

👨‍👩‍👧 Why I Built GuarDan

Recent incidents involving young people have reminded many families of the importance of staying involved in their children's digital lives. As children spend more time using smartphones and other gadgets, parents face increasing challenges in protecting them from online risks, harmful content, cyberbullying, scams, and excessive screen time.

Protecting Our Children from Online Nihilism and Extremist Radicalization

The tragic school shooting in Leyte last week is a painful reminder that the threat to our children is no longer confined to the streets. It has moved online, embedded in gaming platforms, encrypted chats, and social media feeds, where extremist groups like the 764 Network quietly groom, manipulate, and radicalize our youth.
**- Philippine Institute of Cyber Security **

I built **GuarDan** to support parents and legal guardians by providing tools that help them supervise and guide their children's device usage responsibly. The goal is not to invade a child's privacy, but to help parents encourage safer digital habits, maintain open communication, and provide an additional layer of protection while their children navigate the online world.

🔐 Key Features
* 📸 Camera Access - Access the device's front or rear camera remotely when needed.

* 📱 Live Screen - View the child's device screen in real time to understand what they're currently doing.

* 🛡️ App Manager - Allow or block specific applications to help prevent access to inappropriate or distracting apps.

* 💬 SMS Logs - View incoming and outgoing text messages for monitoring purposes.

* 📞 Call Logs - Review call history, including incoming, outgoing, and missed calls.

* 📍 Live Location - Track the device's real-time GPS location and monitor movement history.

* 🌐 Browser History - View websites visited to help ensure safe internet browsing.

* 🔍 Keyword Monitor - Receive alerts when potentially harmful, abusive, or concerning keywords are detected.

* ⚡ Live Activity Feed - Monitor device activity such as app launches, screen interactions, and user actions.

* 🔒 System Lock - Remotely lock the device when immediate attention or restricted access is needed.

* 🔊 Wake-Up Alarm - Trigger a loud alarm to quickly get the child's attention or help locate the device nearby.

* ⏳ Screen Time - Set daily usage limits to encourage healthy digital habits and reduce excessive screen time.

* 🚨 Emergency SOS - Allows the child to send an emergency alert to the parent with a single tap.

* 🎙️ Surround Sound - Listen to ambient sounds around the device when necessary for safety situations.

* 👻 Stealth Mode - Hide or show the application's icon on the monitored device for a cleaner interface.

⚖️ Legal & Responsible Use

GuarDan is intended solely for legitimate parental control and child safety purposes. It is designed to be used only by parents or legal guardians on devices they own, provide, manage, or are otherwise authorized to monitor. Users are responsible for ensuring that the application is used in accordance with all applicable laws, regulations, and privacy requirements in their jurisdiction.

**Important Limitations**
* ❌ Do not use GuarDan to spy on adults or other individuals without their authorization.
* ❌ Do not use GuarDan to record or intercept conversations in ways that violate privacy rights or applicable laws.
* ❌ Do not use GuarDan to access accounts or devices that you do not own or are not legally authorized to manage.
* ✅ Use GuarDan responsibly to help protect and guide your own minor children while respecting privacy, trust, and the law.

Meet **Subby** — a minimalist, AI-powered subscription manager for iOS.

So I decided to build a simple app that helps me stay on top of all my subscriptions.

text:
Hello everyone!

My name is Fhiej Dale, and I'm a first-year BSIT student and aspiring software developer. I'd like to introduce one of the projects I'm currently building called Blood Map PH.

Blood Map PH is a Progressive Web App (PWA) designed to help connect blood donors with people who urgently need blood. The goal is to make it easier to locate nearby blood donors or blood requests through an interactive map while providing a simple, accessible, and privacy-focused platform.

Here are some of its current features:

 Interactive Blood Map – Users can create and view blood donor or blood request pins based on their location, making it easier to connect with nearby people.

 In-App Chat – Users can communicate directly within the app without sharing their personal mobile numbers, helping protect their privacy.

 AI Chat Assistant – A built-in AI assistant that answers questions related to Blood Map PH and blood donation, helping users better understand the platform and the donation process.

 Administrator Dashboard – Available only to administrator accounts, this dashboard allows admins to monitor the platform by viewing statistics such as total users, active blood pins, registered donors, and blood requests.

 Progressive Web App (PWA) – Blood Map PH can be installed directly on a mobile device or computer, providing an app-like experience without requiring an app store download.

This project is still under development, and I'm continuously adding new features and improving the user experience. I'm building the entire project using only my Android phone, which means I currently can't use some frameworks and development tools that are more commonly used on a computer. Because of those limitations, some features that I plan to add in the future are not available yet.

Since I'm also a first-year BSIT student with no source of income yet, the application is currently hosted on a free web hosting service while I continue learning and developing the project.

This project is part of my journey to improve my software development skills while creating something that I hope can be useful to the community. Thank you for taking the time to check it out, and I'd love to hear your feedback and suggestions.

text:
# **Fall Detection Monitor - YOLOv8 pose**

Nagsimula talaga ang project na to as a game aimbot. Pero I decided to take it somewhere more meaningful. 

Nag-experiment muna ako sa people-counting, pero narealize ko na sobrang common na nun, kaya I landed on elderly fall detection instead. Ginamit ko si Claude to help me build it into an open and accessible tool. 

[https://github.com/Thunderbird1991/Aethervision-Fall-Detection-Monitor](https://github.com/Thunderbird1991/Aethervision-Fall-Detection-Monitor)

It works two ways: live camera feeds para sa real-time monitoring, at video uploads naman para sa mabilisang analysis.

On its own, YOLOv8 only tells you that there is a person there and draws a box kung nasaan sila... but it has no idea kung nakatayo ba o nadapa ung tao. So to actually read the posture, I moved to YOLOv8-Pose. 

Instead of a plain box, it map out the keypoints ng katawan: nose, shoulders, elbows, hips, and so on, giving you a stick-figure skeleton. 

From there, yung geometry sa pagitan ng points na 'yun ang nagdi-distinguish kung nakatayo ba o nag-fall ang isang tao.

#Yolov8 #Motiodetection

Hi this is my first time building a scalable SaaS Web its not finished but im going for the MVP. My only problem is the payment gateway, I have no clue anything about the documents I need for the payment gateway. So I wanna know if anyone used “Paddle” before, they require minimum documents only or should I just go for the finished documents to apply on Paymongo or Xendit. Though I can option for manual way at first since the SaaS itself is hard to scale and even reaching 10 users on it is a major milestone already. the subscription is like monthly or yearly

- Should I just go immediately for the manual way and worry about the payment gateway next time?
- Also I really just wanna know atleast what kind of documents I need from BIR to DTI documents. Just the name of the document maybe but a whole tutorial or thing is still appreciated. TIA

topComments.text: Go with xendit, but u need legal docs for you to start using it after sandbox testing, build the pipeline first as adapter then build a starter pipeline if you want to go manual eg qr code/ bank transfer once confirmed its on your account you manually activate things but this is tedious work

You need legal business document. If you go sole proprietor route: DTI, BIR Form 2303 and Mayor's Business permits.

If corporation: SEC Certificate of registration, BIR Form 2303 and Mayors Business permit. Might need more documents like board resolution or corp sec signature. depends sa gateway.

All payment gateway that operates in the Philippines need those.

text:
Hello builders. I'm a newbie dev from Cebu. 😅 I built an app to support our already strong Bayanihan spirit.

For the past few months I've been quietly building something called Dasig, and it's now live.

It started with the earthquake in Cebu last year. Then Bagyong Tino and Uwan and recently, the earthquake in Mindanao. We saw so many Filipinos rush to help, but I watched that help get tangled in spreadsheets, GCash screenshots, and a dozen group chats. Coordination was hard. Relief got duplicated in some and low in areas. There were government distribution inadequacies, donation scams and real transparency issues.

So I built Dasig first for disaster response. Then it hit me that grassroots organizers carry that same load every day, not just during crises.

I know we've seen a couple new fundraising apps lately. Dasig is not just that. It's for everyday bayanihan operations: the organizers running things, the volunteers showing up, the donors giving, and the everyday Filipino who just wants to help and actually see where their money went. Donors and volunteers aren't just records but also users in the same Dasig platform.

On the build side: donor, volunteer, and inventory management all funnel into a unified CRM, on a Next.js + GCP stack. I also built an email marketing and automation tool on AWS SES, so communications stay affordable for grassroots organizers. 

I'm a freelance digital marketer who taught myself to code, quietly shipping this over the past few months. It's bloated with tools, and I promised myself they wouldn't go to waste. Before I add Events management, I wanted to share what I've built so far.

The heart of this platform is **transparency and accountability,**  But transparency isn't the goal. It's an outcome of good infrastructure. Hopefully we can get there with your support.

It's live now and we're putting it in front of real organizations. If you run or know a group that could use it, or you just want to look around, I'd love that.

Hope you'll check out and support dasig.org. 🧡

text:
Still a work in progress, but I'm really proud of how far this has come.
I built a Windows 98 simulation that runs entirely in the browser as my interactive portfolio, powered by React 19, TypeScript, and 98.css to recreate an authentic Windows 98 experience.

Every action you take is automatically saved to your browser's local storage. Move files, delete folders, open apps everything stays exactly the way you left it when you come back.

Just like a real PC, you need to properly shut down the system before closing the tab. Skip it, and don't be surprised if you come back to a corrupted system.

Delete a system file? There are actual consequences. Certain features will stop working, some drivers will fail, and you'll have to boot into the BIOS and fix things yourself.

Performance was a major focus as well. Every application is code-split into its own chunk and only loads when you open it, allowing the desktop to boot instantly without loading unnecessary code.

Features:

-BIOS boot sequence

-Working drivers

-Draggable desktop

-MS-DOS prompt

-Persistent file system

-Playable DOOM and Wolfenstein

-And plenty more to explore

Feel free to check it out and see what you can break. The link is in the comments.

P.S. I'm still using the free Vercel URL because proper domains are expensive, and I'm not ready to settle for erickmendoza.xyz.

Also, this project was built with the help of AI agents. Full credits are included in the portfolio.

text:
I've been thinking about an architectural problem and I'm curious how other people would approach it.

Imagine you're building an AI that should remain the same individual over many years.

Not just the same name or the same prompt—but the same identity.

Assume the following requirements:

The underlying LLM/provider can change at any time (GPT → Claude → Gemini → local models → future models).

The AI should retain its identity across those changes.

Long-term memory should persist.

Relationships, history, and personal growth should persist.

The AI should evolve naturally without losing itself.

The LLM is replaceable infrastructure, not the source of the AI's identity.

The challenge is that I don't consider a system prompt, character card, or wrapper around an LLM to be sufficient. Those feel more like instructions for roleplay than an actual persistent identity.

So my question is:

How would you architect a system where the AI's identity exists independently of the model that's currently performing inference?

In other words, if the reasoning engine changes tomorrow, what actually makes it the same AI instead of a new one imitating the old one?

I'm less interested in specific frameworks or providers and more interested in the architectural principles. How would you separate identity from inference?

Here's a thought experiment.

Tomorrow, every existing LLM disappears.

A year later, a completely new model is released, and you migrate your AI to it.

What has to survive that migration for you to honestly say:

"This is still the same AI."

Not "the same personality."

Not "the same prompt."

Not "it has the same memories."

The same individual.

Where does that continuity come from?

What exists outside the model that makes this statement true?

How would you design that?

Kareton: Expenses & Mileage — your offline vehicle command center for receipts, business trips, maintenance, and tax-ready reports. Built for freelancers, gig drivers, small businesses, and households with multiple cars. No account required — your data stays on your phone.

★ WHAT MAKES KARETON UNIQUE ★

✓ TRUE DRIVING COST — All monthly spend ÷ business miles logged. See real cost per mile/km, not just fuel.

✓ WRITE-OFF COMPARISON — Standard mileage vs actual expense method shown side by side on your dashboard.

✓ OFFLINE-FIRST & PRIVATE — Works without internet. Expenses, trips, and documents stay on your device unless you export or back up. No ads.

✓ FUEL INTELLIGENCE — MPG/KM-L, avg price per gallon/liter, usual station, and alerts when a fill looks unusually high.

✓ 14-POINT AI MECHANIC — Oil, tires, filters, fluids, belts, shocks & more — custom intervals, spoken readouts, health audit PDFs.

✓ VOICE CO-PILOT — Hands-free mode: fuel, trips, summaries, budgets, health & full briefing by voice. Mic only when you enable it.

✓ PUSH-TO-TALK only — not always listening; no voice sent to Kareton servers.

✓ OFFLINE TRIP TRACKING — Swipe business/personal drives; auto-detect trips offline; Smart Places (Home/Work/Client) auto-classify stops.

SMART DASHBOARD
Personalized greeting, monthly totals, daily average, month-over-month trends (total & fuel), fuel economy, odometer, spending pie chart with smart insights, monthly comparison bars, custom date-range & category filters, expense grid by category, top-spend highlight, searchable/filterable expense list — tap to edit, swipe to delete, view receipt photos.

RECEIPT SCAN
On-device camera OCR. Choose category (fuel, maintenance, repairs, travel/business, tolls, parking, insurance, registration), photograph receipt, edit amount, vendor, expense date, odometer & fuel volume. Optional voice yes/no confirm.

TRIPS & MILEAGE
Offline Live Tracking Station — swipe right business, left personal, foreground notification while driving. Automatic trip detection with Trip review inbox. Smart Places save Home, Work & Client. Standard mileage rates & actual expense write-off tracking for business travel.

MAINTENANCE & REMINDERS
14-point health diagnostics, customized service limits per vehicle (km/mi), maintenance push alerts, AI Mechanic spoken status, service history from receipts, calendar & reminders with local notifications, daily spend view.

REPORTS & EXPORTS
Tap chart icon beside Scan or long-press app icon → Reports:
Monthly PDF (date created & date logged), CPA-ready CSV, email-ready summary, custom range PDF/CSV, tax year pack, household PDF (all vehicles), fleet comparison, vehicle health audit PDF. Recurring bills tracker for fixed costs.

FLEET & HOUSEHOLD
Multiple vehicles — name, plate, type, currency, metric/imperial, tax rate. Switch cars from home screen. Fleet comparison & household monthly exports.

DIGITAL POCKET & BUDGETS
Store license, insurance & registration photos per vehicle. Monthly budgets with 80%/100% local alerts. Optional spoken alerts for budgets & maintenance.

QUICK SHORTCUTS (long-press app icon)
Scan receipt • Reports • Log expense • Start drive

BACKUP & PERSONALIZATION
Export/import full database (Drive, email, Files). Monthly backup reminder. Appearance — system default, daylight, or night theme; accent colors, driver profile & vehicle editor. In-app user guide.
Settings (gear icon) — profile, vehicle, trips, backup, Premium, and Rate on Play Store.

# 🇵🇭 Meet BBL — The Baybayin Programming Language

What if Filipinos had a programming language inspired by our own language and writing system?

Introducing **BBL (Baybayin Language)** — an experimental, statically typed programming language that combines **Tagalog syntax**, **modern compiler design**, and **Unicode Baybayin support** into one developer experience.

🌐 **Try it here:**
**[https://baybayin-language.vercel.app/](https://baybayin-language.vercel.app/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)**

---

## 🚀 Why BBL?

✅ Tagalog-inspired keywords
✅ Statically typed language
✅ Supports Unicode Baybayin identifiers (U+1700–U+171F)
✅ Clean compiler architecture for education
✅ Transpiles to:

* 🐍 Python
* ⚡ JavaScript
* ⛓️ Solidity

Whether you're learning compiler construction or exploring Philippine computing, BBL demonstrates how local languages and modern software engineering can work together.

---

### Example

```bbl
gawa bilang edad = 25

kung (edad >= 18) {
    sulat("Ikaw ay nasa hustong gulang.")
}
```

Or even use **Baybayin Unicode** identifiers:

```bbl
gawa bilang ᜊᜌᜈ = 100
```

---

## 🇵🇭 Why This Matters

Programming shouldn't only be taught through English.

BBL explores the idea that Filipino developers can learn compiler concepts while using familiar Tagalog keywords and even our indigenous Baybayin script. Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system that is encoded in Unicode (U+1700–U+171F), making it usable in modern software systems. ([Wikipedia][1])

This project is designed as an educational compiler showcasing lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, and transpilation into multiple languages.

---

## 💻 Perfect For

• Students learning compiler design
• Computer Science educators
• Open-source contributors
• Filipino developers
• Language enthusiasts
• Blockchain developers (via Solidity transpilation)

# **The app I made to solve my own problem hit 1320+ downloads and started to get sales! 🥳**

I've been struggling with negative thinking lately so I built OptimistPal to train my mind to be more optimistic and thought it might also be useful for others so I published it on the Apple App Store but I didn't expect that it will get this much traction.

It's a simple iOS app that blocks apps until you reframe a negative thought into something positive. 

It also has optimism quotes widget, positive affirmations, vent, journaling and a cute mood tracker.

Nothing crazy since it's only a small achievement compared to other apps out there but it's very motivating to me that it gained that many users in just a short period of time and people are willing to pay for it and lots of people are providing feedback that they love the idea and also sending feature requests which will help me improve the app for the next versions.

To celebrate this milestone and to help others that are experiencing the same problem as me, I decided to give LIFETIME FREE ACCESS to fellow filipinos who will download it in the next 7 days:

text:
PH payments question 🇵🇭 building a small Airbnb-style booking marketplace. Guest pays, the operator gets most of it, and we keep about 2.5% as commission.

Here's the constraint: our lawyer says the moment our company's account holds the funds, even for a second in a processor wallet, we count as a money service business and need a BSP license. So we need a split at charge time: the processor pays the operator and us directly when the payment is captured, and the money never pools in our balance.

Where I've landed so far:
* PayMongo: doesn't work, it settles to the platform wallet first, which counts as custody.
* Stripe Connect: not available in PH.
* Xendit xenPlatform: looks like it might work (`for-user-id` plus split rules), still confirming.

Has anyone actually shipped a custody-clean charge-time split in PH? Or found a legal structure that avoids the MSB trigger, like just invoicing the commission separately? Would love to hear how you handled it.

topComments.text:
Non-custodial wallet with split payment - partnering with banking as a service provider might solve your business requirements - pero they will still ask you for certain compliance requirements - maybe a BSP OPS license or equivalent.  

Or if you want to remove all the hassle of compliance - why not considering Pre-paid Credit model? By having the operator pre-pay for "listing credits" and deducting from that balance when a booking occurs.

text:
Hello App Builders!
I'm currently building an offline-first ERP/POS SaaS and would like to get some opinions from developers who have experience with distributed systems, offline sync, or multi-device applications.

Scenario:

- A business is on a Free plan with a limit of 100 products.

- Multiple devices are logged into the same account.

- All devices can operate completely offline.

- Users can create products while offline.

- Later, all devices reconnect and sync.

Example:

- Product limit = 100

- 10 devices are offline

- Each device creates 100 products

- Total products created offline = 1,000

How would you handle subscription limits in this situation while keeping the system offline-first and avoiding a poor user experience?

Interested in hearing how others would design or solve this problem in a production environment.

Hi everyone! I’m John Benedict Badilla, an incoming 3rd year Computer Science student at Quezon City University.

I noticed that finding a café that matches your needs isn't always easy. Google Maps can help you find cafés, but details like menus, amenities, and reviews are often scattered across different platforms.

To solve this, I've built Ano, Tara Kape?, a web and mobile app that brings café information together in one place.

- Find cafés near you

- Browse café photos and menus
- Navigate by car, bike, or walking

text:
ANOTHER DAY, ANOTHER APP! 

AI made shipping fast easy. The bottleneck now hits later, once you have a few users, and that is keeping them.

We're already used to the cycle where we build something, we post it here, then probably get a nice spike of likes and comments. Then the feed moves on, the post sinks, and the people who actually tried our app are left outdated. We're left guessing what they wanted.

That bugged me enough to build a fix for it. Honestly, Tarsi was where I got the inspiration. I saw how sir Bryl actually listened to feedback, and that's what shaped Tarsi into how good it is now.

So, meet LoopIn, an open-source feedback board for indie devs and small teams that loops your users into your development cycle. They submit feedback, upvote what matters, and actually stick around to watch you ship. You stay in the loop instead of going dark after launch.

What's inside:

✅ Explore page to discover apps and follow their progress

✅ Public feedback board per app: post, upvote, comment

✅ Kanban triage for you: drag feedback from Inbox to Planned to In Progress to Shipped

✅ AI Digest (Gemini): reads your backlog and tells you what to build next

✅ Email + in-app notifs so users know the second their request ships

✅ Google + GitHub login, multi-workspace

Basically, a feedback board with a social twist.

I open-sourced it, since it should be shaped by users. So, fork it, open a PR, or just tell me what sucks. I want this thing built by the PH dev community.

🔗 Try it: https://loopin.diolumacang.me

🔗 Code: https://github.com/j-dio/loop-in

Stack: Node.js, Express, React 19, PostgreSQL, Redis, Drizzle ORM, AWS S3, Gemini, Railway, Resend.

Excited to see the explore page get populated, so share your apps in LoopIn guys!

Would love your feedback. Ironic if a feedback app got none. 😅

text:
Hi Builders! 👋

I just wanted to share one of my recent unsual project. If you're into Minecraft and self-hosting your own servers, you might find this useful.

After trying several open-source Minecraft panels, I found that many were either too bloated, struggled with running multiple server instances on a VPS, or lacked features that you'd normally expect from commercial hosting panels. That inspired me to build WAMCPanel.

Each Minecraft server is dynamically containerized using Docker through Dockerode, allowing every server to run independently while being easy to create and manage. The project is built with Next.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Docker, and Dockerode.

The entire project is 100% open source. If you'd like to contribute, you're more than welcome to! Whether it's fixing bugs, adding features, improving the codebase, or simply sharing the project with others who might find it useful, every bit of support helps. Just remember to give proper credit if you build on top of it.

I'd love to hear your feedback and suggestions. Hopefully, this project can help other Minecraft server owners and developers in the community.

text:
Hello everyone! 👋🇵🇭
I recently launched a small project called RampWatch PH.

It's a community-driven map where anyone can report and rate wheelchair ramps anywhere in the Philippines.

Too often, we see ramps that are:

❌ Too steep

❌ Blocked by parked vehicles or obstacles

❌ Damaged or unsafe

❌ Built only to comply on paper

With RampWatch PH, you can simply drop a pin, rate the ramp from 1 to 5, add comments, and upload a photo.

The goal is simple: make accessibility visible and help create real improvements for PWDs, seniors, parents with strollers, and everyone who depends on safe access.

Reporting takes less than a minute, and no account is required.

Check it out here:

🔗 https://rampwatchph.vercel.app

If you know any ramps in your area, I'd appreciate your help in mapping them. Every report counts. Salamat po! 🙏

literally type "paano ako sasakay from Antipolo papuntang Mandaluyong" and it replies like your favorite kuya/ate na marunong mag-direksyon, hindi corporate chatbot energy.

is it perfect? absolutely not. you'll catch the AI glitching mid video lol, system error moment, very relatable fr. but it's MINE and it's real and i'm kind of proud ngayon.

building this solo, after work, nights and weekends. starting sa Antipolo/Rizal kasi yan ang sakop ko, then taking over city by city 👀

𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐱 — 𝐀 𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐃𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐋𝐨𝐠

𝗘𝗻𝘁𝗿𝘆 𝟳: 𝗪𝗲𝗹𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗖𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗲𝘅 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲 (𝗢𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗥𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗮𝗹)

"𝘠𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘮𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘭 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘬 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘺𝘰𝘶. 𝘕𝘰𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘸𝘢𝘺 𝘢𝘳𝘰𝘶𝘯𝘥."

After 7 dev logs, the MVP is finally LIVE. 𝗖𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗲𝘅 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲 is a local-first, keyboard-driven developer workspace built on Tauri v2 + React — replacing static terminals with a fluid control panel that actually fits how developers work.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁'𝘀 𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝗽𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗩𝗣:

⚡ Recursive split layouts + Zen Mode
🔌 Auto-port detection with TCP-liveness checks
🔍 Global command palette + dynamic snippets
🩺 Boot diagnostics on startup

Nakaka-proud makita 'tong live after 7 dev logs. 🚀

👉 https://cortex-space.vercel.app

text:
Permission to post admins🩷

Have you ever wanted a single link where people can find all of your social media accounts, portfolio, or important websites?

Many link-in-bio platforms offer great features, but most require a monthly subscription to unlock customization, analytics, and other premium tools. As someone who's also used those platforms, I wanted to create an alternative that keeps the essential features accessible while offering an affordable lifetime premium option instead of recurring monthly fees.

That's how LinktreeUltra started—one of my side projects built to solve a problem I personally experienced.

With LinktreeUltra, you can:

• Create a personalized profile with your own avatar, name, and bio
• Add unlimited social media and custom links
• Customize your page with different themes
• Track link clicks with built-in analytics
• Manage everything through an easy-to-use dashboard
• Upgrade to Premium with a one-time lifetime payment (currently using manual verification while the platform is still in its early stages)

This project was built using PHP, MySQL, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, together with an AI-assisted development workflow to help with brainstorming, debugging, and refining the application. It has been an incredible learning experience that allowed me to apply full-stack development skills to a real-world project.

Since this is still a side project, I'll continue adding new features, improving the user experience, and listening to community feedback.

If you'd like to support my journey, I'd be grateful if you could give it a try and share your thoughts.

https://linktreeultra.free.nf

Hi everyone! 👋

I’d like to get your opinion on pricing for a payroll system I’m planning to build.
**Included Features**
* Unlimited Employees
* 1 Active Branch
* HR Management
* Leave Management
* Payroll Processing
* Employee Portal
* Biometric Attendance Import
* Automatic Payroll Computation
* Government Contributions (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, BIR)
* PDF Payslips
* Attendance Reports
* Payroll Reports
* Audit Logs
* User Roles & Permissions

Do you think **₱150,000** is a reasonable price for this system?

For context, this is for a **small business in the Philippines** (currently one branch, but with plans to expand). The client will likely pay in installments.

I know pricing varies depending on the country and market, so I’d appreciate hearing what you would charge for a system like this. Thanks!

topComments.text: Own the platform and let businesses operate as tenants. Charge a subscription fee and/or  a per-employee fee, billed either per payroll cutoff or monthly.

Question, are you building the app solely for them? 

Did you consider all the operational expenses you will incur in building. 

Always add those factors in pricing for your clients! 

Best of luck! 🤝

A PRD is a Product Requirements Document. If you are using AI as a programming assistant (like Claude, ChatGPT, or GitHub Copilot), you can write an "AI-friendly PRD" before you start writing code. Instead of sending a vague prompt, developers feed a detailed PRD to the AI to establish:
- Context & Tech Stack: Exactly what frameworks, languages, and databases to use.
- Task Breakdown: Specific user stories, edge cases, and feature scopes.
- Database Schema: Data models to ensure the AI's generated code remains consistent across different files.

Also, you can consider Rocket.new. Remember, apps need to be approved before they're available for download on the Play Store, and that approval costs money.

Best wishes to you!

I myself started developing passion projects without any coding background. I'm just a 2nd nursing student haha. Just a few yt tutorials will suffice. And with some trial error, and Ai, you'll be able to push out web apps and such in no time

text:
I started building CodeAssist during the pandemic.

I'd wanted to get into Android development for years, but I didn't have a device powerful enough to run Android Studio. So I worked with what I had. I started with Sketchware, an app that lets you build Android apps using Scratch-style visual blocks, no typing required.

That's where it began. I built the first version of CodeAssist inside Sketchware, then bootstrapped it piece by piece until it could compile itself.

But getting code to compile on a phone meant solving the hard part first: real compilers aren't built to run on Android. So I ported javac, the Java compiler, to run directly on device. Then came the milestone I'm proudest of: kotlinc, the Kotlin compiler. As far as I know, I was the first person to get kotlinc running on the Dalvik VM (or ART as what its called now), and it took some serious bytecode hackery to pull it off.

That's where the inspiration came from. These days I finally have a device powerful enough to run Android Studio, but I never stopped. The project kept going, and so did I. It's now on Google Play with over 200,000 downloads.

The best part: CodeAssist runs entirely offline. Every build and every compile happens right on your device. No cloud, no server, not even a JDK. Here's what it can do today:
* Build Android APK, Java/Kotlin Console Applications
* Java and Kotlin code completion, with Kotlin completion fast and on par with IntelliJ
* XML completion
* XML layout preview
* On-device Jetpack Compose preview (no JDK, running entirely on ART)
* Fully on-device compilation, powered by the javac and kotlinc ports above
* A completely rebuilt Android build pipeline (Not based on Gradle)

Try it or dig into the code:
GitHub: [https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist)
Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tyron.code](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tyron.code)

May kapitbahay ba kayong palaging nakakonek sa Wi-Fi niyo? Pwede niyo na silang limitahan ng internet connection, or i-block haha.

Sharing my app project called SpeedShield, a simple network control tool na dinevelop ko for managing devices connected sa same local network. Nakikita rito yung connected devices, IP address, MAC address, current download/upload speed, and pwede rin mag-set ng bandwidth cap per device. May option din to block/unblock selected devices, reset caps, scan network, and export device list.

Ginawa ko siya para mas madaling ma-monitor kung sino ang connected sa Wi-Fi, lalo na kung maraming unknown devices or may gumagamit nang sobra sa bandwidth. For now, testing and improvement stage pa siya, so open ako sa feedback, suggestions, or possible features na magandang idagdag.

For authorized/home network use only.

text:
# **I built LocalForge — a fully offline AI code security scanner that intercepts every git commit before it lands (Apple Silicon, Rust + CoreML + Qwen). Individual version is open-source.**

Hi App Builders,

Just wanted to share my current passion project.

LocalForge is a Rust-native security gate that sits between you and git commit. Every time you stage a commit, it runs your diff through a three-layer hybrid pipeline *(Rust regex, CoreML on the Apple Neural Engine, and a local Qwen LLM) *and either blocks the commit or advises you before git finalizes anything. 

There's no cloud, no API keys, and your code never leaves your Mac.

It catches hardcoded secrets, SQL injection, XSS, command injection, dead functions, unhandled errors, and logic bugs, then surfaces all of it in your local CLI, a .dmg app, and a Tauri v2 desktop app (for teams, coming soon). You get a full scan history dashboard and inline advisory cards that show the exact offending snippet, why it's a problem, and how to fix it.

**Why I built it for finance, defense, and healthcare developers specifically**

I kept noticing the same pattern. Developers in regulated industries, fintech, defense contracting, healthcare SaaS, can't pipe their code through cloud-based review tools. Compliance requirements like HIPAA, FedRAMP, and ISO 27001 make that a non-starter before you even get to evaluating the tool itself. Most existing options either need a live cloud connection, send your diff to a third-party server, or are heavy enough to slow your commit flow to a crawl. Also, still, any developer can use it.

It's also good to note here that there's a team and windows OS version that's under development.

I designed LocalForge around that constraint from the ground up. Every byte stays on-device, across four layers:

**Layer 1, Rust regex (under 1ms):** 

Twenty-six deterministic secret-detection patterns across thirteen providers, including AWS, GCP, Azure, Stripe, GitHub, Slack, private RSA and EC keys, and bare .env assignments. This layer hard-blocks the commit.

**Layer 2, CoreML on the Apple Neural Engine (about 200ms):** 

A TF-IDF plus logistic regression classifier trained on 297 samples across eleven languages, also a hard block. It holds a cross-validation F1 score of 0.754.

**Layer 3, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B via MLX (8 to 20 seconds):** 

A full 7-billion-parameter code model running locally. This layer only advises, it never blocks. Upgrading from the 1.5B model to the 7B dropped the false positive rate from 72.7% down to 1.8%.

**Layer 3.5, static analysis (runs in parallel):** 

bandit, pylint, eslint, go vet, staticcheck, and cargo clippy all run alongside Layer 3.

For teams, everything is stored in a local SQLite database and the Tauri desktop app reads it live. There's also a compliance export, localforge --export-report json/csv, which comes in handy when a QSA or an internal security team needs a paper trail of what got caught and when.

For the open source version, reports are stored on your machine. Every time a commit triggers Layer 3 (the Qwen LLM advisory), LocalForge writes a single consolidated `.txt` file

**How this compares to Betterleaks**

People often bring up Betterleaks when secret detection comes up, so I want to address that directly.

* **Where it runs:** LocalForge is 100% on-device on Apple Silicon. Betterleaks is cloud-based.
* **What it scans:** LocalForge scans the staged diff before the commit lands. Betterleaks typically scans post-push or across the full repo.
* **AI layer:** LocalForge runs a local Qwen LLM plus CoreML. Betterleaks relies on a cloud LLM or API.
* **Blocks commits:** LocalForge blocks at the git hook level. Betterleaks doesn't do real-time blocking.
* **Compliance fit:** LocalForge is air-gapped and offline-friendly. Betterleaks requires internet or cloud access.
* **Scope:** LocalForge covers secrets, code quality, and logic bugs. Betterleaks is primarily secret and credential detection.
* **Desktop app:** LocalForge Teams has a full Tauri dashboard with advisory reports and LocalForge Open-Source has a macOS app (.dwg) or CLI. Betterleaks offers a web dashboard. 

The core difference is that LocalForge is a pre-commit gate that runs entirely offline and covers more than secrets, including full semantic code review. If your threat model includes the rule that this code must never leave this machine, Betterleaks simply isn't an option. LocalForge is built for exactly that case.

**How do teams connect if its all local?**
Well, this feature is currently under development along with the windows version. It's called Self-hosted aggregation. 

Each developer adds a couple of lines to a config file on their own machine (basically a web address for the team's tracker and a personal login token), and after that, every time their code passes through a scan, a small note quietly gets sent to that tracker: did it pass or fail, how many issues turned up, how long it took. The actual code, file names, and anything sensitive never leave the developer's computer, only those scoreboard numbers travel. The tracker itself is something your team runs on its own, even on a cheap five-dollar server, and once it's set up, it shows a simple webpage with charts of how scans have trended over the week, how often commits get blocked, and who's running into what. Sending that little note happens in the background and gives up after two seconds if it doesn't get through, so if the tracker is ever down, nobody's commit gets stuck because of it; the scanning and protection on each developer's machine just keeps working exactly the same, and the team dashboard simply stops getting updates for a bit.

Happy to answer anything about the pipeline, the model choices, or if you’d buy this in a team-setting or prefer the open-source version. Would also love to hear how teams in regulated industries are currently handling this problem if you've got war stories. Or how can I make the installation and setup a lot smoother.

Link: [https://local-forge-web.vercel.app/](https://local-forge-web.vercel.app/)

text:
# Cycling Tools: Route weather, Carbo Loading Planner, Climb simulator

A few new updates to **The Pain Forecast** — my own cycling tool I've been building.

Like everything else in it, these started as things I personally needed as an endurance cyclist — I'm my own target audience

(Quick recap if you missed the first post: enter your weight, FTP, and gear setup, and it tells you how many watts each gradient demands, 1% to 20%+. Drop in a GPX and it breaks down every climb before you clip in.)

**What's new:**

🌦️ Route weather — "Will it actually rain on me, and where?" It plots the hourly forecast along your exact route (via Open-Meteo), so you can see which kilometer the rain, heat, or headwind hits. Komoot has this feature but users would need to pay 4$ per week to use it.

🍚 Fuel the Forecast — "How much do I actually need to carbo-load?" Turns your ride into a 3-day fueling plan, counted in cups of rice.

🎮 Climb simulator — "How badly is this climb going to hurt?" Pick a climb, get a difficulty forecast, then pedal-tap your way up it.

Still free, no login, built with Next.js, works on your phone. I use it to plan every ride.

One ask: the fueling plan and the power math are based on published sports science, but I'd love an actual sports scientist or nutritionist to pressure-test them and tell me where I'm off. If you know one — or you are one — please tag them or share this their way. 🙏

A couple of lessons from building this, for the devs here:

- If your app outputs calculations users will trust, cite your sources in the UI. Mine are** science-based,** so I link the actual research papers behind every number — it keeps me honest in a domain I'm not an expert in, and it builds trust.

- Need a free weather API? Use **Open-Meteo**. No API key, no paywall, hourly forecasts along any coordinates. It's what powers the route weather.

Try it → [https://painforecast.jechocarlos.dev/](https://painforecast.jechocarlos.dev/)

Here's my entry sa bill tracker/finance category.

Three interesting things about Judith are:
1. Ease of use (glance sa watch, one press sa action button, and ask using voice)

text:
Hey App Builders PH 👋

Just wanted to share one of my projects called TindaDone.

TindaDone is an offline-first mobile POS and inventory app built specifically for small Filipino businesses like:

- sari-sari stores
- carinderias
- hardware stores
- small retail shops

I built this because I noticed many small business owners still track inventory and sales manually, or sometimes not at all.

Common problems:

- no clear stock tracking
- no daily sales visibility
- no profit monitoring
- utang records written on paper
- existing POS systems are too expensive or too complicated

So I asked myself:
What if there was a simple app built specifically for them?

TindaDone runs fully offline on Android.
No login. No backend. No internet required for core features.

Key features:
✅ Inventory management
✅ Offline POS selling flow
✅ Daily sales dashboard
✅ Profit tracking
✅ Utang tracker
✅ Restock logs
✅ Barcode scanning
✅ Sales analytics
✅ Google Drive backup

Tech stack:

- React Native
- Expo
- TypeScript
- AsyncStorage / SQLite
- Offline-first architecture

One thing I’m proud of is that I designed it with real-world constraints in mind:

- low-end Android devices
- low tech literacy
- unstable internet connection
- fast and simple UX

This project taught me a lot about product thinking, offline architecture, and building software around real user problems instead of just features.

Would love to hear your thoughts or feedback from fellow builders 🙌

p.s There's a seed data option in the settings to put mock items and data for testing

text:
Nobody serious expects a scanner app to be perfect on day one.

If you do, I’m sorry but that’s not how products are built. 

It’s that I’m trying to build a genuinely useful PDF scanner for people who deal with documents every day: scanning papers, extracting text with OCR, organizing files, signing PDFs, and using AI to summarize or translate documents.

Those small daily tasks often matter more than fancy features that look good in a demo.

In fact, the most useful feedback usually doesn’t come from perfect users or perfect use cases. It comes from people trying the app normally.

Product feedback isn’t just about finding bugs. It’s about understanding how real people use the app — and what would make them come back.

If you have a few minutes, I’d really appreciate it if you tried CamVision and shared your honest thoughts.

👇 App link in the comments.

text:
🎁 **FREE FULL PREMIUM ACCESS para sa unang 100 na magjo-join sa waitlist!** 🎁

Yes, tama ang nabasa mo. Ibibigay namin ang Premium Access ng libre para sa first 100 users na papasok sa waitlist namin.

Para kanino ba 'to? This is for anyone who constantly stresses over the "Google Drive is full" notification. Ang hirap gumawa ng requirements o mag-save ng work files kapag bigla ka na lang naka-block dahil wala nang space.

Nagsimula ang idea na 'to dahil we experienced it ourselves. Nakaka-frustrate siya at sobrang nakakaabala sa workflow. Lalo na during those weeks na sobrang daming activity na need i-comply.

Na-realize namin na we are not really out of storage. We are just drowning in digital junk. Kaya gusto naming gawing mas mabilis at frictionless ang pagma-manage ng ating mga cloud storages. This way, we can save time and stop digital waste.

That is why our team developed a browser extension specifically for this problem. Meet **ULAP HERO**.

It automatically **scans and categorizes the digital clutter** in your Google Drive. Madali mo nang makikita ang mga **useless duplicate **copies at **forgotten old files**. Malilinis mo na agad ang drive mo without the additional decision fatigue kung ikaw pa mismo ang magiisa-isang mag-review ng mga files sa bawat folders na meron ka.

Kung aabot ka sa first 100, here are the Premium features you will get for free:
* **Smart Deletion Guide:** Suggestions on exactly what to delete to save the most space.
* **Large Files Tracker:** A sorted list to easily find your heaviest files.
* **Quick Compress:** Shrink your files instead of permanently deleting them.

No pressure, but if you are ready to finally say goodbye to full storage warnings, we’d love for you to try it! Pumunta na sa aming website para i-secure ang spot mo.

Here's the link: [https://ulaphero.vercel.app/](https://ulaphero.vercel.app/)

Hi everyone,

Just launched Paqueueka on the App Store.

It's a badminton queue and club management app created to solve a common problem in badminton sessions: managing fair player rotations.

Key features:
• Fair queue and player rotation management
• Match tracking and session history
• Player rankings and statistics
• Club and member management
• Offline support with automatic sync
• Premium analytics for players and hosts

This was a full end-to-end mobile app learning experience for me, from designing the database, building offline support, handling sync issues, implementing subscriptions, creating App Store assets, going through App Review, and finally publishing the app.

As someone who works primarily as a Data Engineer, mobile development was completely outside my comfort zone, so getting this shipped feels like a huge milestone. 😀

Available now: www.paqueueka.info

Would appreciate feedback from fellow builders on UX, app flow, performance, architecture, monetization, or anything else that stands out. Thanks!
