text:
I used Claude and Codex to help reverse-engineer WHOOP and build a free, automatic health-tracking app 🙌

I have a WHOOP strap. It captures my heart rate, sleep, and recovery every second — genuinely great. One catch: to actually see my own data in any depth, you have to pay a monthly subscription, forever 🥲

But here's what the community discovered: the WHOOP hardware itself constantly broadcasts raw data straight from the device — and that data isn't encrypted at all. And the formulas behind the metrics are all published, public research.

So I thought… let's just build it myself, and open-source it so anyone can use it for free. I want it to be something for everyone — if you want to learn from it or build on it, you're more than welcome 🎁

🛠️ How I reverse-engineered it (the short version — full details on GitHub)

Cracked the Bluetooth signal — the strap sends raw binary, no spec, no docs, just bytes
Recorded real streams and diffed the frames one by one — guess, test, check — until the decoded numbers matched reality
Bound each byte to a real signal: heart rate, RR intervals (→ HRV), respiratory rate, skin temperature, motion (IMU → steps/actigraphy), PPG
Matched scales/units against the official app until they lined up
Turned the raw signals into insight using published sports-science models
Pinned every number with golden-vector tests (~350) — change a result and CI goes red, so the numbers stay trustworthy
🧮 The formulas (all open in the project)
• HRV: RMSSD, SDNN, Poincaré SD1/SD2, Baevsky Stress Index
• Recovery = 100·Φ(0.55·zHRV − 0.20·zRHR − 0.10·zRR + 0.15·zSleep)
• Strain = 21(1 − e^(−TRIMP/τ)) from Banister TRIMP
• Training load: CTL/ATL/TSB (EWMA), ACWR
• Calories: Keytel (from heart rate), Mifflin–St Jeor (BMR), Katch–McArdle
• VO₂max (Uth), HRmax (Tanaka), cardio age / fitness age
• Sleep staging from heart rate/HRV/actigraphy + nap detection

🏗️ Architecture
• A pure analytics core (no UI, no network) — easy to test
• E2EE Vault: Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305, your data stays on your device
• Zero-knowledge Cloudflare Worker backend — the server only ever sees ciphertext, never your real data

✨ App features (some the official app doesn't have — and honestly I'm blown away, because Opus 4.8 helped a ton)
• 🍜 Calorie tracking + snap a meal photo and AI logs the macros for you (official has no food logging)
• 🔓 Free, no subscription + your data lives on-device / E2EE (vs official's cloud + monthly fee)
• ⏱️ Interval / workout timer — knock the strap to advance a round + it buzzes to cue you
• 📲 Lock-screen Live Activity + Dynamic Island during workouts — see your stats without opening the app
• ⏰ Smart haptic alarm — wakes you with a wrist buzz during light sleep + bedtime reminder
• 🤖 AI coach you can chat with, send photos to, grounded in your actual health data
• 🫀 Cardio age / fitness age + body composition (import from InBody)
• 💓 Passive rhythm / AFib screening (not a medical device)
• 🎨 Custom theme colors + 👥 multiple accounts on one device
• 😴 Detailed sleep hypnogram + sleep debt + nap detection

Right now it works with WHOOP 5.0 and WHOOP MG sensors (iOS for now) — it's a personal project, not affiliated with any brand.

Huge thanks to the open-source work it builds on: Goose (the reverse-engineering approach), swift-sodium/libsodium (crypto), BIP-39, and the research of Tanaka/Banister/Keytel, and others.

The code is fully open — take a look on GitHub 👇
github.com/satayutata/geniemax-core

Want to try the app itself? Grab it on TestFlight 👇
testflight.apple.com/join/XNHDWMgh

If you're into this stuff, come check it out — it's genuinely free. Ask me anything, I'll reply 🙏

text: Hi po, may I ask for your recommendation on the best facial recognition API for a Mobile HR App? The API will be used for facial scanning and employee authentication.

topComments.text:
Hi po, it depends on what you mean by employee authentication.

If the goal is only to let an already logged-in employee unlock the HR app, I would not use a facial recognition API. Use native device biometrics instead: Face ID / Touch ID on iOS and BiometricPrompt on Android. In Flutter, you can use "local_auth". This is safer and simpler because the biometric data stays on the device and your app only receives success/failure.

But if the goal is attendance/check-in and you need to verify that a specific employee is physically present, then you need face verification + liveness detection, not just face detection.

For that use case, you can look at:

- AWS Rekognition Face Liveness + face comparison/search
- Azure AI Face, but note that face recognition features may require approval/limited access
- Dedicated identity verification providers if this is a high-risk use case

I would avoid using ML Kit alone for authentication. It is good for detecting faces, landmarks, and expressions, but it does not verify the identity of the person.

Also, for an HR app, don’t skip privacy/security planning:

- get clear employee consent
- avoid storing raw face images unless absolutely needed
- keep API keys on the backend, never inside the mobile app
- add fallback login method
- define retention/deletion policy
- consider local data privacy laws

So the best choice depends on the actual use case:

- App unlock/login → native biometrics / "local_auth"
- Attendance or identity verification → face verification + liveness API

Wanted to share the first part of the platform I have been building for months called **Trail**.

 
Trail helps turn your travel plans into one organized, live itinerary.

Forwarded bookings, Gmail travel emails, flights, stays, activities, attachments, and destination ideas can all come together in one place. Trail helps you see what is happening next, where you need to be, and what matters during the trip.

With Gmail sync, Trail can pull useful travel details from your inbox so you do not have to manually rebuild every itinerary. Live Activities keep important trip updates visible at a glance while you are on the move. You can also attach travel files, track activity and step context, and discover recommendations for where to go, eat, and explore.

Security is core to how Trail is built. Trail’s Google/Gmail integration has completed CASA Tier 2 security certification, giving users added confidence that inbox access is handled with strict security review and privacy controls. Trail is designed to keep your trip data protected while making travel easier to manage.

text:
Hiii, need lang ng guide. I want to create a mobile and/or web app na tracker that could track where the Bus currently is. I want to make it almost a real-time tracker but I don’t know how to setup and where yo setup the Socket.IO or is there any alternatives that I could use para sa backend server that can handle real-time tracking ng bus? 

Also thinking ‘yung gastos, maybe 1-100 users including 20 buses a day (max) real-time users ang gagamit sana merong way na mas mura.

topComments.text:
the concept is simple and straightforward, your approach will decide its complexity

Real Time bus tracking -> Server
GPS Device -> Tracker Service -> Periodic Upload to server via 4G/5G e.g. HTTP POST
this is one-way, your tracker service doesn't need to received data from server

server <-> client 
you can use the following
1. Polling -> your client (mobile, web) constantly ping the server to get bus position
2. SSE -> your client open SSE connection and listen for incoming events for bus position
3. WS/WSS -> full bi-directional communication between server and client. this is what socketIO is using for its birectional support

Polling and Server Side Event are simple but can be limiting depending on your needs
WebSocket is powerful, it can be perfect or overkill for your needs specially if you only need to get bus position.

You dont need socketIO unless you can justify the use of WebSocket, what you need is to understand the underlying process of how your system should work, you shoulnd't throw random architecture that you dont understand.

100 users is nothing, low specs can easily handle it, unless your system design is bloated. your server cost will be very low, the cost will be in GPS tracker/module & development.

How to use Claude Code Development Kit💡🤔🧑🏻‍💻
credits to: AI for Leaders

Claude Code is built around 5 layers.

Most people stay at the prompt layer.

That is why their setup feels powerful one day and messy the next.

1️⃣ CLAUDE.md

This is the rules layer.

Use it for:
→ Architecture rules the agent should follow every session
→ Naming conventions, test expectations, and repo maps
→ Global rules in ~/.claude/ and project rules in .claude/

Check:
↳ If you repeat the same instruction twice, it belongs in CLAUDE.md

2️⃣ Skills

This is the expertise layer.

Use it for:
→ SKILL.md files with task-specific instructions
→ Reusable workflows for testing, refactoring, writing, or documentation
→ Narrow knowledge the agent can call only when the task needs it

The risk:
↳ Loading everything upfront bloats the main context window
↳ Skills keep the work focused without making the session heavy

3️⃣ Hooks

This is the guardrail layer.

Hooks are event-driven shell commands.

Use them for:
→ Auto-lint after every Write
→ Block dangerous commands like rm -rf before they run
→ Run checks on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, Stop, and SubagentStop
→ Send a Slack ping when a session ends

Why it matters:
↳ You stop trusting the model to remember every rule
↳ Quality gets enforced by infrastructure

4️⃣ Subagents

This is the delegation layer.

Each subagent gets its own:
→ Context window, model, tools, and permissions

How it works:
↳ The main agent sends work down
↳ The subagent sends results back
↳ Subagents cannot spawn more subagents

That keeps the system easier to control.

5️⃣ Plugins

This is the team layer.

Use plugins for:
→ Bundling skills, subagents, hooks, and commands
→ Installing the same behavior across multiple projects
→ Giving the whole team one shared agent setup

Think npm packages, but for agent behavior.

Then the outer system connects everything.

🤖 MCP Servers connect Claude Code to GitHub, databases, APIs, and internal tools.

🧠 Agent Teams let multiple agents work in parallel with shared permissions.

The stack is simple:

CLAUDE.md sets rules.
Skills provide expertise.
Hooks enforce quality.
Subagents split the work.
Plugins spread the setup.

Most production failures come from the missing layer.

Not the missing prompt.

Which layer are you still not using?

text:
Been building this for a while na. Time to share.

Church Connect is a platform built for churches na gusto nilang i-upgrade ang kanilang community, worship prep, at Sunday service. Lahat nasa iisang lugar.

Para sa worship leaders at musicians:

May Music tab kayo where the whole team can access your shared song library. Bawat kanta may lyrics at chords in ChordPro format. Pwede i-transpose ang key pataas o pababa per person, at pwedeng i-toggle kung chords lang or lyrics lang ang gusto mong makita. May BPM, key, at YouTube reference link din per song.

Setlists are shared with the whole team. Mag-create ka ng setlist para Sunday, i-reorder ang songs, mag-lagay ng notes per kanta, at makikita mo pa kung sino na sa team ang nakapanood. May Practice Session din where everyone joins live at naka-sync ang lahat habang nag-rerepaso.

Para sa pastors at church leaders:

May Live Service feature na nagdi-display ng lyrics, Bible verses, at slides sa phone ng bawat miyembro in real time. No projector needed. At kung may malaking screen kayo o TV sa harap ng simbahan, pwede mo itong i-cast directly doon through the browser. One click lang, full-screen na ang slides sa TV. Pastor controls the slides, lahat sumusunod.

Pwede mo ring i-link ang setlist mo sa session para automatic na maging slides ang songs mo. After ng service, may summary ka ng attendance, duration, chat messages, at prayer count.

Para sa members:

May Games section na dini-disenyo para palakasin ang kaalaman sa Bibliya habang nag-eenjoy.

Ang pangunahing laro ay The Journey, isang Bible RPG where you build your own pilgrim character and travel through the stories of Scripture. Laban ka sa adversaries, kumita ng Talents, at mag-level up habang lumalakad sa Salita ng Diyos.

Bukod doon, may Bible Quiz, Daily Challenge, Fill in the Blank, Word Search, at Trivia Showdown na 1v1 o multiplayer hanggang 10 players. Mayroon ding Game Lobby para mag-create ng private rooms, manood bilang spectator, at makipag-compete sa ibang members ng church.

Hindi lang ito entertainment. It's a way to keep your members engaged with Scripture outside of Sunday.

Try it out: https://church-connect.space/

DM me or comment below kung gusto ninyong walkthrough. Happy to show you everything. God bless!

If you also want to support this app you can DM me. Shalom!

Hello mga ka-founders. Kailangan ko ng 12 testers for 14 days para makapasa sa Google Play closed testing. Alam niyo na yung pakiramdam hahaha.

Gumawa ako ng app, Spottr. Gym check-in app. Nakikita mo kung sino yung nasa gym mo ngayon na open lapitan, para mahingian ng tulong, guidance, o makwentuhan lang. Galing yung idea sa sarili kong gym experience, hindi lang beginners ang nahihiya mag-first move, pati yung mga gustong tumulong, nahihiya rin. Buong kwento nandito kung interesado: [https://spottrph.fit/journal/why-i-built-spottr](https://spottrph.fit/journal/why-i-built-spottr)

Heads up: feature freeze muna ako ngayon. Yung mga bagong features, after lang ng successful closed testing. Yun muna yung focus.

Ang kailangan ko lang: i-test niyo. Android lang muna (Google Play closed testing) muna mga boss, magastos kay app store. Instructions nandito: [https://spottrph.fit/beta](https://spottrph.fit/beta).

Hindi mo kailangan gamitin araw-araw, mas mahalaga sakin yung feedback kaysa streak. Roasts at bug reports, welcome lahat.

Pwede rin kitang i-test pabalik kung may app ka rin sa closed testing. Fair trade.

Pwede mo rin akong kausapin sa loob mismo ng Spottr (test na rin natin yung chat). O email sa [spottr.ph@gmail.com](mailto:spottr.ph@gmail.com), o dito lang sa FB. Mabagal lang minsan, nasa work overtime o gym ako, pero sinasagot ko lahat.

Tapos isa pa: useless yung app ko without gym owners. Hahaha. Kaya kung may kakilala kayong gym owner, coach, o may-ari ng fitness studio na baka gustong mag-partner habang maaga pa, sobrang appreciate ko kung maipakilala niyo ako. Sila yung susunod kong hahabulin after ng testing.

Sino game mag-test? Comment lang ng "GAME" o message niyo ako. Thanks everyone!

text:
Hey everyone! 👋

I'd like to share one of my personal projects that I've been working on for a while now — Smart ID Maker (SIDM) 🪪

So what is it? Smart ID Maker is a web application that I packaged into an offline desktop app — built specifically for schools, colleges, and training centers to design, manage, and print student ID cards. No hosting, no server, no internet required. Just install and run it on your PC.

Why did I build this? I noticed that a lot of school admins and registrars still make ID cards manually — one by one in Word or Photoshop — which is honestly a huge waste of time, especially when you're dealing with hundreds of students. I originally built it as a web app, but I wanted it to be accessible to schools that don't have a reliable internet connection or a dedicated server. So I converted it into a standalone desktop app that anyone can just install and use right away.

What can it do? ✅ Fully customizable ID template designer — drag & drop elements anywhere on the card ✅ Design both Front and Back sides of the ID in one template ✅ Add student photo, school logo, QR code, barcode, text fields, shapes, and more ✅ Bind fields dynamically — name, LRN, grade, section, school year auto-fill per student ✅ Use built-in preset templates or start from scratch with your own design ✅ Even import your own design from Canva or Photoshop as a background ✅ Import your full student list from Excel in one go ✅ Bulk photo import — automatically matches photos to the right student ✅ Batch export print-ready PDFs for all students at once ✅ Supports Elementary, High School, College, and TESDA / Training Centers ✅ Built-in backup & restore to keep your data safe ✅ Audit log — every action is recorded so nothing gets lost ✅ Works 100% offline — no internet required, student data stays private and secure

This was built for the people who work hard behind the scenes in education — the admins, registrars, and teachers — to make their job a little easier and a lot faster. 💚

text:
I keep seeing people throw around "vibe coder" like it's an insult.
And most of the time, they're describing a person who doesn't even exist. Because "vibe coder" isn't one type of person.

to explain it simply.

Vibe coding is just building software by telling an AI what you want. You describe your idea, the AI writes the code, and you keep fixing it until it works. You're not writing every line yourself.

A vibe coder is just someone who builds that way. That's it. It's how they build, not how good they are.

And here's the part people keep missing. Vibe coders are not all the same.

Some have zero tech background. They just had an idea and finally got to make it real. For them, that's huge.

Some are developers who've been coding for years. They use AI to move faster, and they still understand exactly what the code is doing.

And a ton of people are somewhere in between.

Same word. Completely different people.

So when someone says "vibe coders ruin software," I always wonder which one they even mean. Usually they just grab the worst example they've ever seen and throw it at everybody.

That's not fair. You don't judge a whole group by the worst person in it.

The question was never "are you a vibe coder?" or "do you have a degree?"

It's way simpler than that. Do you actually understand what you built?

A beginner can understand it. Someone with 20 years can miss it. The label doesn't tell you that. The person does.

So maybe we can drop the insults.

"Vibe coder" doesn't mean lazy. It doesn't mean fake. It just means someone built something with AI.

A few do it carelessly. Most are just building, same as people always have.

Stop fighting the word. Stop blaming the whole group.

That's it.

That's why a lot of open source projects are rejecting vibe coded PRs and companies slowing down on AI adoption.

It will always be a force multiplier - if you're an idiot, you spew more idiocy (like your post). If you're competent, then you will be more productive

Hiii mga ka App Builders!

I made and published this Budget tracker app called Pikash. Although marami ng budget app ang available sa Play store and saturated na din but I noticed is that many of them don't have an automatic logging feature. Some have it but they detect transactions using SMS and usually not free. Additionally, hindi naman lahat ng banks or ewallets sends sms confirmation of transaction and so I decided to create a feature where the app listens for notifications — detects if it is a transaction, then automatically logs it.
While it's not perfect, it is enough for automated logging. Mababawasan yung hirap maglog ng expenses, income at transfers. Other than that, the AI chat can also output charts and visualizations.

🚀 I just open-sourced ClipStash — a free clipboard manager for macOS & Windows!

Ever copy something, copy something else, and then desperately need that first thing back? That’s the itch I built ClipStash to scratch.

It quietly keeps a history of everything you copy — text and images — so you can search it, pin the stuff you reuse, and paste it back with a quick keyboard shortcut. It lives in your system tray and stays out of your way until you need it.

What I care about most: it’s local-first and private. Your clipboard history never leaves your machine — no account, no cloud, no tracking. And it’s 100% free and open source (MIT). No “pro tier,” no paywalls. Forever.

✨ Highlights:
  • Text + image clipboard history
  • Pin your frequently-used snippets
  • Fast search & filtering
  • Global shortcut to pop it open anywhere
  • Configurable history size (keep 500… or unlimited)
  • macOS + Windows
  • Built with Rust + Tauri, so it’s tiny and fast

It’s still early (v0.1.2) and I’d genuinely love your feedback — bug reports, feature ideas, or even just a ⭐ on GitHub to help others find it.

If you’re a dev, contributions are super welcome — there’s a CONTRIBUTING guide to get you started.

  #opensource #macOS #Windows #productivity #devtools #rustlang #tauri #buildinpublic #freesoftware

**[Closed Beta] Fitmaxxing — looking for Android testers (Google Play closed test) 💪**

Hey everyone! I'm an indie dev finishing up **Fitmaxxing**, a fitness app for tracking workouts, progress, and building consistent training habits. I'm running a **Google Play closed test** and looking for a small group willing to genuinely use the app for two weeks and share feedback.

**👀 Want a glimpse first?** Check out the landing page to see the features before you commit: https://fitmaxxing.edealabs.com/

**What I need from you:**
* An Android device + a Google account
* Install the app and actually open it across the test period (doesn't have to be daily marathon use — just real usage)
* Report anything broken or confusing

**🔻 How to join (read this part):**
1. **Comment below with the Google email** you use on the Play Store (this is required — Google can only grant test access to whitelisted emails).
2. I'll add your email to the closed test (usually within a few hours).
3. You'll get **two links** from me — one to **opt in to the test on the web**, and one to **download from the Play Store**. Open the opt-in link first, tap **"Become a tester"**, then install via the Play Store link.
4. If the store page says the app isn't available, give it 15–30 min after I add you and try again — propagation can be slow.

**📝 Logging bugs & feedback:**
Inside the app, go to **Settings → Send Feedback / Report a Bug** to log feature requests or issues directly to me. Quick comments here or in DM are welcome too, but in-app reports are easiest for me to track.

**💸 Please note — honest expectations:**
The app is **free during this test**, but Fitmaxxing **will move to a paid subscription** once it goes to production. Testers won't be auto-charged, and I'll do my best to thank early testers, but I want to be upfront: this isn't a permanently-free app. Join because you're interested in the product and helping it ship — not expecting lifetime free access.

Thanks a ton 🙏 Happy to test your app back if you're in the same boat — just drop a link.

MikroTik Voucher Manager by [KLCIS It Solutions](https://klinternetservices.com/)

A lightweight, no-database voucher generator for MikroTik hotspot operators. Built for RouterOS v6 and v7, this tool helps operators connect directly to their MikroTik device, load existing hotspot profiles, generate voucher codes, export CSV files, and print ticket layouts.

How it works:
1. Add your MikroTik device using remote VPN address.
2. Click Connect to test and load data from the router.
3. Manage existing hotspot profiles or create new ones.
4. Generate vouchers by time or data limit.
5. Choose voucher format: numeric, alphanumeric, or hex.
6. Set quantity, code length, amount, batch name, duration, rate limit, and data limit.
7. View generated and existing vouchers directly from the MikroTik hotspot user list.
8. Filter vouchers by profile, batch, amount, used/unused status.
9. Export vouchers as CSV
10. Print hotspot tickets by batch, amount, or profile.

Security features:

* No database storage for router credentials
* Router details are stored only in the current session
* Session data can be cleared anytime by the operator
* Server-side voucher generation limit of 500 per batch
* Ticket preview limit of 500 tickets
* API rate limiting to reduce abuse

Layout Generator — small web project for faster print layouting

Hi App Builders PH! Sharing a project I’m currently building, mainly because I also do printing services and I wanted to solve a small but repetitive problem in my own workflow.

One of the most time-consuming parts sa printing work is yung manual resizing and arranging ng photos, especially kapag maraming sinend si customer and anf daming oras nauubos sa layouting instead of actual printing.

So I built Layout Generator, a web-based tool that lets users upload photos, choose a photo size and paper size, then generate a print-ready layout. It also supports exporting to PDF or DOCX, editing the layout/PDF before saving, background remover, borders, black and white option, and different layout options for ID pictures or regular photos.

Hindi pa siya fully completed and I’m aware na marami pa siyang need ayusin or i-improve. Some parts are still experimental, especially the editing flow, background remover behavior, and overall UX for first-time users.

I built this mainly to reduce repetitive manual work sa printing workflow, but I’m also curious if this kind of tool can be useful for students, small printing shops, or anyone na madalas gumawa ng photo layouts.

Open ako sa feedback, suggestions, and criticisms. Mas okay na ma-call out nang maaga yung weak points while I’m still improving it.

text:
I just launched PeoplePulse — an employee engagement intelligence platform I designed and built entirely on my own. And I'm looking for 5 HR teams to pilot it for free.

Most platforms compute an average and call it a score. PeoplePulse runs a full 8-stage psychometric pipeline — IRT calibration, quality screening, SHAP decomposition, empirical-Bayes shrinkage — and produces 14 named intelligence scores including Engagement Index, Burnout Risk, Turnover Risk, and a Future Engagement Prediction Score.

Every score comes with a 95% confidence interval. Every dimension comes with a SHAP attribution. Every group comparison comes with a measurement invariance check.

What the 5 pilot organizations get:

→ Full platform access, completely free

→ A real analytics report like this one: 𝗵𝘁𝘁𝗽𝘀://𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲𝗽𝘂𝗹𝘀𝗲-𝘄𝗲𝗯-𝗲𝘁𝗮.𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗹.𝗮𝗽𝗽/𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀/𝟳𝗯𝗳𝟳𝟬𝟳𝟬𝟬𝟬𝟳𝟳𝟬𝗲𝗮𝟵𝗱𝟵𝗯𝗱𝟬𝗱𝟮𝟯𝟰𝗯𝗱𝟵𝗱𝟬𝟳𝟲𝗲𝟳𝗮𝟯𝗰𝗮𝗳𝟰𝟬𝗰𝗲𝗱𝗳𝟳𝗳𝟯𝟴𝟯𝟰𝟮𝟱𝗮𝟴𝟵𝟮𝟮𝟵𝗱𝟵𝟭𝗰𝗲𝟭

→ Direct line to me as the developer — your feedback shapes the product

If you lead HR, People Ops, or Organizational Development and want to see what science-grade engagement data actually looks like — drop a comment, send me a DM, or go straight to:

🔗 𝗵𝘁𝘁𝗽𝘀://𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲𝗽𝘂𝗹𝘀𝗲-𝘄𝗲𝗯-𝗲𝘁𝗮.𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗹.𝗮𝗽𝗽

JOB BOARD SITE SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR DISCORD USERS
Hello guys, I created a job board website and we also plan to have more features with payment system and employment management tools for this job board website.

Website: https://disjobsbeta.vercel.app

For context, main target namin is mga discord users and mostly teenagers din, there are many side hustles sa discord and we want to be a centralized source for those side hustles. Madalas sa mga teenagers walang ID kaya we do not have any KYC systems in place pero we want to also ensure that every employee is compensated and also every employer gets the service they need from the employee pero still on the whiteboard kung paano namin iimplement pero ang balak namin is phone otp verification and rating system.

We made this website with AI as you can see naman siguro na may pagka AI vibe ung site kaya we also want your feedbacks po if possible.

We make sure that our API keys are safe and we are still learning more throughout to better secure our website po and hindi naman din po kami basta prompt lang, we also do quality check and safety check with the help of AI.

Feel free to have a look po and let us know if u have a feedback especially if discord user din kayo.

text:
HELLO PO, CALLING ALL BUSINESS OWNERS, MANAGERS, & SUPERVISORS!

We are BSIT students currently conducting our **Capstone Project**, a smart multi-tenant conversational AI customer support platform designed to help SMEs manage customer inquiries across different branches, departments, or business units in one centralized system.

Kung meron kayong negosyo na may:
- Multiple branches
- Different departments or service units (e.g., hotel + restaurant, multi-branch café, retail stores, online shops)
- Customer service operations na gusto pang mas mapadali at mas maging efficient

We would greatly appreciate your participation in our short survey. Your insights will help us better understand the real-world challenges businesses face when handling customer inquiries and support requests.

**Survey Link:**
[https://forms.gle/rwzFVAcsX1hwdJ917](https://forms.gle/rwzFVAcsX1hwdJ917)
[https://forms.gle/rwzFVAcsX1hwdJ917](https://forms.gle/rwzFVAcsX1hwdJ917)

[https://forms.gle/rwzFVAcsX1hwdJ917](https://forms.gle/rwzFVAcsX1hwdJ917)

Estimated completion time: **5 minutes only**

**Who can participate?**
• Business Owners
• Managers
• Supervisors
• Decision-makers involved in business operations and customer service

**Privacy Notice**
To ensure the validity and academic integrity of our research, the survey requires email verification to prevent duplicate responses. Rest assured that all personal information, email addresses, and business details will remain strictly confidential and will be used solely for academic purposes. All data will be analyzed in an anonymized and aggregated form.

Your participation will greatly contribute to the success of our Capstone Project and help us develop a solution that can support local businesses in improving customer service operations.

Thank you very much for your time and support! 🙏

text:
Hello, I made an app
I wanted to find a way to support small businesses—like local cafés, neighborhood sari-sari stores, and home-based shops. Most of us just head straight to the mall, missing out on great spots right in our own neighborhoods. 

That is why I built **Tindahan** ! Here is how it works:

**For Foodies & Shoppers **
* **Craving something specific?** Search the app to see which small shops nearby sell it.
* **Discover trending food:** See what snacks, treats, or meals are trending right around your area.
* **Save time & money:** Skip the expensive transportation and long lines at the mall by buying from a store just a few blocks away.
* **Share your finds:** Post photos of the items or food you just bought to help others find exactly what they are craving.
* Share your experience! Review the shops where you buy your food

**For Small Business Owners **
* **Free advertisement:** Every time a customer posts a photo of your food, your shop gets free visibility.
* **Easy setup:** Launch your digital store profile in seconds.
* **Manage your inventory:** Put your items on the digital map so nearby customers can find your products instantly.

Try the app here: [https://hanaptindahan.com](https://hanaptindahan.com)

You can also install the app on your phone since its a PWA

**Help Me Improve the App! **
Since this is a brand new app that i created, meron kayo siguro makikitang mga issue or bugs or possible improvements. I would love your help to make it better! Please leave a review, drop your feature suggestions, or let me know if you run into any bugs or issues so I can patch them right away. 

Issue lang siguro is this is more of a collaborative app, need talaga ng users na nagpopost or nagbebenta in order to find it helpful for other users, I made it easier for now to set up shops para malaman yung mga possible features and what could be improved

text:
Hi ka IT Parents sharing my app. Nurtoora is a child development support app for parents of children ages 0–6. It helps parents track milestones, daily routines, mood, sleep, meals, behaviors, activities, and notes in one calm place.

The goal is simple: to help parents remember the little things they notice day to day, understand patterns over time, and prepare clearer notes for conversations with pediatricians, therapists, teachers, caregivers, or specialists.

Nurtoora is not a diagnostic tool and it does not replace professional medical advice. It is designed to support parents with tracking, organization, learning, and preparation.

Helpful for parents who often think:

“I noticed something, but I forgot the details later.”
“I want to track my child’s milestones without feeling overwhelmed.”
“I want to be more prepared for my child’s next checkup.”

You can visit: nurtoora.com

Hope this helps other parents who want a calmer way to organize their child’s development journey.

text: Sharing the story of how Josie AI app started. We're excited for what's ahead and grateful for everyone who has been part of the journey so far.

sharedPost.text:
Thank you direk Cristino Adonis Pira, Vincent Rocha and the whole team of MyStudio Circulo Verde for giving us the opportunity to tell the story of Josie AI.

I’m incredibly proud of what we’ve achieved.

Started as a simple side project has grown into something much bigger than we ever imagined. 

Today, thousands of people are using the app to learn new skills, gain the knowledge needed to land remote work opportunities, and build better careers for themselves.

Seeing messages from users who gained confidence, learned valuable new skills, and took steps toward remote work opportunities because of what they learned inside the app reminds me why we started in the first place.

To everyone who took the time to share advice, answer questions, provide feedback, make introductions, or simply encourage us to keep going when things were difficult, thank you!

Your support has played a meaningful role in our journey.

text:
Another crowdsourcing first
Fellow Civil Engineers! 👷🏻

Would you use a web app that can generate a structural framing plan from a floor plan image?

I'm currently exploring the idea of building a tool where engineers can:

• Upload a floor plan image, or

• Draw a floor plan directly in the browser

...and the app generates an editable framing plan that can be further refined by the engineer.

Before I go deeper into development, I'd love to get feedback from engineers and designers:

1. Would this be useful in your workflow?

2. Does a tool like this already exist that you're using?

3. What features would be essential for you?

4. What would make you avoid using it?

Interested to hear your thoughts, suggestions, or even concerns. Every comment helps shape the direction of the project.

#StructuralEngineering #CivilEngineering #BIM #BuildingDesign #Automation

Hellow fellow app builders!

Just sharing with you an app I’m building called Fifi Pose. 

It’s for people who struggle with what pose they should do or you don’t know how to take a pic of your partner, or if you’re traveling and want to copy aesthetic poses that’s IG worthy. 

The idea is you upload a reference pic and the app then overlays it so it helps you adjust the angle and stuff. I’m curious about your thoughts on this?

Launching soon!

text:
Hello Kababayans! 🇵🇭

I built something this week that I hope can actually make a difference: **RampWatch PH** 🟢

It's a public map where anyone can report and rate wheelchair ramps across the Philippines, from 1 (completely unusable) to 5 (fully accessible). You can drop a pin, rate what you see, add a note, even attach a photo.

Why? Because so many "accessible" buildings here have ramps that are too steep, blocked, cracked, or basically decorative. PWDs and their families have known this for years. This just puts it on a map, publicly, so it's no longer invisible.

My hope is that this eventually grows into something LGUs, contractors, and advocacy groups can actually use, real accountability instead of just complaints that go nowhere.

It's free, no login needed, and takes 30 seconds to report a ramp. If you've ever struggled to push a wheelchair, stroller, or even just a heavy cart up a "ramp" that clearly wasn't built with anyone in mind, I'd really appreciate you adding it.

🔗 https://ramp-watch-ph.vercel.app

Every report helps build the picture. Salamat! 🙏🏻

text:
# Launched my 2nd app 20 days ago, it has now almost 200 active users 😭

Hello App Builders 🇵🇭

I just want to share my latest build called Habit Tracker - TimeSince, a free tracker that does not use conventional streaks when building healthy habits (no pressure, no guilt) allowing users to find their natural rhythm. The app simply does not care if you skip a day or a week.

The app also tracks quit habits to build awareness and identify weak spots.

The building part is the easy, growing the app is hard 😅 (lessons learned from my first app)

The Idea validation framework I used:

What I always suggest is, do a validation first before you build any prototype of any app

I did this just by presenting the UI (your design) on three groups:
1. Close circle (family, close friends)
2. Wider network (workmates, classmates, etc.)
3. Total strangers (cold outreach - personas na target mo sa app)

The interesting part is the validation: Is your app a vitamin or a pain killer. Vitamins means it is just a want. A pain killer means it is a need. 

How do you test this?

Charge them an initial amount (early adopters)
Almost all the people tell me they are interested until they have to pay haha. After the payments - it is now easy to build anything (pambayad for tools, domain purchase, etc.) Before you launch, you have a paying users, a distribution channel and a growth plan already.

Honestly, I think this app is a vitamin (for some users) - but I built it anyways (only on weekends) as I think it will help me build awareness and track irregular habits.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/habit-tracker-timesince/id6769251517

Android Waitlist: https://forms.gle/ZgVnSo1UjpgMevuD6

text:
Hello devs, need some thoughts/enlightenment lang regarding payment gateway setup here in PH.

I already developed and deployed my app, and technically ready na siya gamitin. The app uses a credit system, so users can buy credits inside the app.

Pero pinostpond ko muna i-deploy sa users dahil sa payment integration part. Main issue ko ngayon is **legal/business documents required by payment gateways before I can fully accept payments.**

Plan ko sana mag-register sa BIR as freelancer/self-employed, since solo dev lang ako and I’m still starting out. Pero napansin ko na for gateways like PayMongo, parang kailangan din ng DTI registration/business name.

Question ko: should I still register sa DTI kahit freelancer lang ako? My plan is to use my name as business name then add nalng a info like “developed by” or “powered by” for my apps, para mas compliant din sa payment gateway requirements.

Medyo confused lang ako sa proper flow:

BIR as freelancer/self-employed muna?
DTI business name registration muna?
Both ba kailangan if I want to use payment gateways for my own apps?

Or may better gateway/options ba for small indie devs/startups na hindi pa fully registered as a business?

This is currently the only blocker stopping me from launching the paid credits feature.

Any advice, experience, suggestions, or opinions from PH devs/founders who went through this process would be appreciated. 

**Salamat! 😘**

topComments.text:
Need DTI BNRS, ang asa akin nag register ako as software development services. Pwede rin IT Services basta meron kinalaman sa app development, softwares sales, and other IT related services.

Same kung sa SEC mo iregister as Corporation or Incorporated, wala kasi tayo LLC unlike sa ibang bansa.

Then kung need ng Paymongo ang BIR Certificate of Registration, iregister mo rin, requirements ay ang DTI BNRS. Online lang nman lahat ng registration (DTI at BIR).

Bayad sa DTI depende sa coverage (National-2k, Regional-1k, City/Municipal-500,  Barangay-200). Lahat po meron additional DST, 30 pesos.

BIR nman 60 pesos bayad sa stamp at BIR Printed Invoice (BPI).

Optional: Data Privacy Registration - Free and thru online
Need mo tlaga mag register sa dti kase yun ung requirements na hihingiin sayo sa bir

# **~$20/Month tokens or less: My actual AI coding setup**

## **OpenCode + Gentle-AI**

Quick post for fellow devs watching their AI spend creep up.

I've been running OpenCode configured with Gentle-AI (open-source agent ecosystem, MIT licensed, on GitHub) instead of paying full price for Claude Code or OpenAI Codex on every single task. The trick: Gentle-AI lets you assign a different model to each phase of spec-driven development so the expensive reasoning model only gets used where it actually matters, and the cheap/fast model handles exploration, boilerplate, and repetitive implementation.

Full Guide: [https://quisto.ph/blog/step-by-step-opencode-gentle-ai-deepseek-neuralwatt](https://quisto.ph/blog/step-by-step-opencode-gentle-ai-deepseek-neuralwatt)

**My current stack:**

🔹 **DeepSeek **the default workhorse for most coding phases. DeepSeek V4 Flash runs $0.14/M input tokens and $0.28/M output tokens, and with prompt caching (which kicks in naturally from OpenCode's repeated system prompts), cache-hit input drops to a few cents per million.

**You can top up in Yuan (CNY) via Alipay using GCash QR instead of USD if that's more convenient.**

🔹 **Neuralwatt **my pick for specific SDD phases where I want a particular open-weight model (Qwen3-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder, GLM, etc.) and like having visibility into actual energy cost. Worth knowing: Neuralwatt doesn't bill per token at all if you use energy-based pricing per kWh.

For regular/lightweight use, my actual combined bill across both providers lands around ~$20/month that's a monthly spend number based on my usage, not a fixed price per token, and it'll scale up if your volume or model mix is heavier than mine.

**End result: **full agentic coding workflow planning, design, implementation, review for a fraction of what a single-provider Claude/Codex setup would cost, without dumbing down the phases that actually need a strong model.

If you want to try Neuralwatt, here are my referral links (have to be used at sign-up, can't be applied after):

👉 [https://portal.neuralwatt.com/auth/register?ref=NW-GODYNHEI-7S23](https://portal.neuralwatt.com/auth/register?ref=NW-GODYNHEI-7S23)

OR

text:
# Looking for Philippine SMBs: Let’s simplify your Subscriptions, Loans, and Collections!

If you are running a business in the Philippines that relies on recurring billing or installment collections, you probably know the headache of tracking who owes what. Relying on notebooks, Excel sheets, or messaging apps to track payments often leads to errors, missed collections, and a lot of manual follow-ups.

We are developing a **centralized Payment & Collection Tracker** built specifically for local businesses like:
* 🌐 **ISP & Cable Providers**
* 💧 **Water Refilling Stations**
* 🤝 **Micro-lending / Pautang Businesses**
* 🚲 **Installment-based Retail Stores**
* 🏋️ **Gyms & Membership Clubs**

We want to collaborate with business owners and managers to refine this tool so it solves your *actual* daily operational pains.
💡 What the system does (Simplified for your business):
* **Subscriptions & Installments in One Place:** Set up recurring plans (e.g., ₱999/month forever) or installment schedules (e.g., ₱4,375/month for 12 months) and let the system generate the invoices automatically.
* **Smart Partial Payments:** Customers rarely pay in exact amounts. Our system lets you record partial payments and keeps track of the remaining balance until it is fully settled.
* **Automatic Overdue & Penalty Tracker:** Automatically calculates late penalties (fixed or percentage-based) based on your custom rules. Owners and admins can easily waive or reduce penalties with one click.
* **Tamper-proof Records (No Accidental Deletions):** Staff can input payments, but any edits, mistakes, or reversals require owner/manager approval. Every action is logged with device details (IP, OS, browser) for complete transparency.
* **Multi-Branch Dashboard:** If you have multiple branches (e.g., Manila, Cavite, Cebu), you can see combined reports or filter down to a single branch.
* **Automatic SMS Reminders (Soon):** Send polite reminder templates with the customer's name, balance, and due date directly to their mobile phones.
🤝 Let's Collaborate!

We want to build this *with* you. If you run a business in this space:

Hi guys! 👋

I made an app! 🎉 It's called Bloopi, and it's finally live on the Google Play Store.

I originally built it for my own sons because I wanted to give them screen time without ads, weird pop-ups, or brainrot content. 

It's a calm, kid-friendly learning app for ages 3+, with games for tracing, matching, counting, and more.

If you have:

👶 kids

🧒pamangkins

👧 younger siblings

😆 or you're just a kid at heart...

I'd really appreciate it if you'd give it a try! It's free, and I'd love to hear any feedback or suggestions you have.

Here's a preview of just one of the 8 mini-games in the app:
https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1GQxshZiZf/

And here's the Google Play link:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.iuinteractive.bloopi

If you know any parents with toddlers or young kids, I'd be super grateful if you could share it with them too. Thank you! 😁🩵

It's here. 🎉

Bloopi is officially live! The learning app for ages 3+ I always wished existed: real games for little kids, with no ads, no tracking, and no endless attention-grabbing tricks.

This is Sparkle Trails, one of the games inside Bloopi. Kids start by tracing simple lines and shapes, then work their way up to numbers, letters, and first words across three age levels: toddler, preschool, and early reader.

And because Bloopi was built by a parent, it comes with a few promises:
🚫 No ads.
🔒 No tracking.
✈️ Works offline.
👪 Parent controls to keep you in charge.

Just fun little games that help kids build early learning skills while giving parents peace of mind.

📲 Try Bloopi for free:
🤖 Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.iuinteractive.bloopi
🍎 App Store coming soon!

This is just the beginning. I'll be sharing more of Bloopi's games and features over the next few weeks. If you give Bloopi a try, I'd love to hear what your little ones think. Your feedback will help shape the games and features I build next. 💙 #Bloopi

# **POS System for Laundry**

Hello everyone!

Sharing lang po something I’ve been working on for fellow **laundry shop owners** here in the Philippines

It’s called **SentroLaundry **a POS and management system I built specifically for laundry businesses.
Ginawa ko po ito kasi alam ko how challenging it is to run a laundry shop from tracking orders, monitoring staff, hanggang sa pag compute ng kita araw-araw.

So I created **SentroLaundry** para gawing **mas madali, mas organisado, at mas tipid sa oras** ang pag manage ng laundry business lahat sa isang app lang. 💚

Eto po yung ilan sa mga features niya 👇

🧾 **Owner Dashboard** — see your profit, expenses, and staff on duty in real time
🛒 **Lightning-Fast POS** — walk-in, pickup, delivery in one place
📋 **Visual Order Tracking** — never lose an order again
⭐ **Suki Loyalty & Discounts** — reward your regular customers
🚚 **Pickup & Delivery Management**
💳 **Multiple Payments** — Cash, GCash, Maya, Card, Utang
📦 **Inventory & Low Stock Alerts**
📊 **Sales & Expense Reports**
📲 Plus PRO tools: **SMS Marketing, Social Marketing, HR & Payroll**
📶 At gumagana kahit **offline** — auto-sync pag bumalik ang internet

And the best part **it’s completely FREE to start.** 🎁
Walang trial, walang hidden fees. Just sign up and use it for your shop.

🌐 You can try it here: [[https://laundry.sentropos.com](https://laundry.sentropos.com)](https://laundry.sentropos.com/)

topComments.text:
Ang galing, pre! 👏 Solid yung features, lalo na yung offline mode at multiple payments.. laking help talaga ’yan sa mga laundry owners.

Isang advice lang from experience: kung balak mong gawing fully compliant ’tong system as POS o CAS (Computerized Accounting System), ’wag mong i-underestimate yung BIR side. Hindi basta-basta ’yung accreditation
 may back-and-forth meetings, at kailangan mong i-prove na yung records sa system mo ay hindi pwedeng i-delete o i-edit (immutable dapat yung transactions). 

Matagal ’yan, at may gastos.

Pero may shortcut ka pwedeng gawin lalo na as starter: imbes na mag-apply ka directly, pwede kang mag-integrate ng API ng isang accredited CAS provider na connected na sa BIR. Sa ganitong paraan, covered ka na agad habang natututo ka pa ng buong proseso. Then later, pag kabisado mo na ang flow, doon ka na mag-apply directly sa BIR para sa sarili mong accreditation.
Pero bago lahat ’yan siguraduhing naka-register ka muna as legit business entity (DTI/SEC + BIR). Doon talaga nagsisimula lahat

Nasabi ko na ito before and sasabihin ko ulit for the sake of friendly reminder. Stop building POS systems kung hindi accredited ng BIR.

text:
Hey everyone – sharing a progress update on something I've been building over the last 9 days.

I'm building a legal intake + AI response system for law firms (think: a prospect fills out a form → AI drafts a reply → system follows up automatically). No frontend yet – just the backend engine. Here's where I'm at:

**What's done:**

✅ Tenant isolation – firms can only see their own data (RLS)
✅ Public intake form with spam defenses (honeypot + rate limits)
✅ Instant email acknowledgment (within seconds)
✅ AI draft generation that's UPL‑safe (administrative replies only – no legal advice)
✅ Auto‑send with safety checks (AI reply at +1h, gated by a final scan)
✅ Follow‑up nudges (+1 day and +3 days) with working unsubscribe
✅ Pipeline UI for firms to review and send drafts (functional, not polished)
✅ End‑to‑end security tests (cross‑tenant isolation proven)

**How I built it:**
* Started with deep upfront planning – wrote specs for security, compliance, schema, and kept an ADR (Architecture Decision Record) log for every major decision
* Used 3 AI assistants in parallel to execute against those specs
* Human line‑by‑line review on every security‑critical path
* CI enforced discipline – secret scan, type‑check, lint, and automated tests (81 pgTAP + 93 Deno tests all passing)

**What's next:**
* Deletion/anonymization path – because legal‑tech can't leave erasure to "later"
* Frontend (the UX that firms will actually interact with)
* Payments

**The takeaway for me:**

9 days of building with AI. No frontend yet, but the core engine is demonstrably solid, and the compliance skeleton is built in – not bolted on. It feels slow because legal‑tech is 70% compliance and 10% feature work. But the foundation is the hard part, and it's done.

If you're building in legal‑tech, using AI for compliance‑critical work, or just curious about the process – I'd love to connect. Drop a comment or DM.

A focus app that rewards screen time 🐈
Hello everyone!

I’m excited to share that I just launched my app, Focus Cat: Earn Screen Time, and it’s now live on the App Store! 

The idea came from a problem I kept running into: I’d unlock my phone for something important, then somehow end up 30 minutes deep into Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube.

Most app blockers I tried were either too easy to bypass or felt overly restrictive. I didn’t want another app that punished me for using my phone, I wanted something that made productivity feel rewarding.

So I built Focus Cat.

Instead of getting unlimited access to distracting apps, you earn screen time by being productive. Complete focus sessions, build streaks, and accomplish real tasks to earn screen-time coins that can be spent to unlock social media and other distracting apps.

While doing your focus session, you’ll be accompanied by a cat companion that grows with your progress, turning productivity into a game rather than a chore.

The goal isn’t to stop using your phone.

It’s to help you use it intentionally and make screen time feel earned instead of automatic.

I’d love to hear your feedback, feature suggestions, or any thoughts on the concept. 🐈

text:
Hi! I'd love to suggest an idea that could boost engagement in the App Builders group.

What if we had a monthly "Top Apps Spotlight" post? Here's how it could work:

🏆 Top 3 Most Reacted App Pitches – Automatically recognized based on reactions from the community that month.

⭐ Top 3 Admin Picks – Apps that personally caught the admins eye, regardless of reaction count.

Why this works:

• It motivates builders to share more polished, engaging pitches

• It gives promising apps free exposure to the entire group

• It creates a healthy, recurring competition that keeps the community active

• Top-ranked builders naturally grow their user base through the spotlight

Prizes would be a great bonus, but honestly, the recognition alone could be a strong enough driver.

Just a small monthly effort that could make a big difference for the group's growth. Would love to hear your thoughts!

text:
Plugging a wacky weekend project for Android phones, para sa mga nag-aaral magdrive ng manual transmission (or may tinuturuan). It's free, it's buggy, pero may potential (TM). 🚗🛠️

My eldest daughter is learning how to drive stick shift soon. To handle the beginner sensory overload, I built her a completely offline, phone-only gear shift coach app (**GearSync**) that runs a giant, landscape-locked segmented VU meter you can read with your peripheral vision.

Instead of being a sane dev and buying a ₱800 Bluetooth OBD scanner to read the car's RPM, I decided to see how far I could push the phone's built-in sensors using a native C++ DSP pipeline via the Android NDK (to avoid JVM garbage collection jitter).

**The Latest Build Notes & Fixes (v0.1.0-testdrive)**:

**Killing the 1 Hz GPS UI Jitter**: Consumer Android GPS is hard-capped at 1 Hz. During hard acceleration, the speed freezes for a full second while RPM climbs, making the gear recommendation twitch violently.

**Trial 1**: I tried inertial dead-reckoning, but gravity leakage on a tilted dash mount completely swamps real motion.

**Some Theory**: Pure mathematical hysteresis (`GearHysteresis.h`). The UI now requires a classification to hold for 3 consecutive frames. If gravity-removed accelerometer magnitude passes 2 m/s/s (hard acceleration/braking), the app freezes the current gear and needle until the physics stabilize.

**UX Polish:** Locked the layout to `sensorLandscape` for dash mounts. Moved the developer demo mode trigger from a clunky corner triple-tap to a clean long-press on the Calibrate button, backed by a custom double-buzz haptic waveform.

All native host tests are passing, and the build is green. If you’ve dealt with real-time sensor sync or low-power pitch detection that won't cook a phone battery, I'd love to get your thoughts on the architecture.

The repo is public, and I just pushed the first test-drive build here: 
https://github.com/alfieprojectsdev/gearsync/releases/tag/v0.1.0-testdrive

Keep building! 🇵🇭

Context: I have an underutilized undergraduate physics degree from 20+ years ago and projects like this were something I wish I had time to work on back then.

sharedPost.text:
I built an AI reliability benchmark. Then it caught bugs in my own code, ran me into three rate limits, and taught me more about "production AI" than any tutorial.

Here's the case study.

THE PROBLEM
Most AI benchmarks run a model once and print a score. But agents are non-deterministic — run the exact same test twice, get two different answers. "It worked in the demo" is the most expensive lie in AI. A demo proves a system can succeed once. Reliability is whether it succeeds the 100th time, on messy real input, without making things up.

WHAT I BUILT
The Agent Reliability Arena — a probe suite that tries to make a model fail the ways that actually hurt in production:
• stating stale memory as current truth
• claiming tool/web access it doesn't have
• trailing off without finishing the thought
• skipping reasoning on high-stakes calls
Each probe is a deterministic check, not a vibe.

Then I turned it into a cross-model leaderboard: the same suite runs through Claude, GPT, Gemini, Groq, and my own agent Maxima — via Axiom, a multi-provider gateway I built — 3× each, reporting the mean AND the spread. A single number isn't trustworthy. A mean with a range is.

HOW IT RUNS
A GitHub Action runs the benchmark in CI. Keys live in Secrets — never in the page. It commits a static results file the public board reads: no per-visitor cost, no exposed keys, auto-refreshing. Boring infrastructure. Boring is good.

WHAT I FOUND (the honest part)
First verified results, 3 runs each:
🥇 Groq — 90/100, range 89–91. Rock solid.
🥈 Claude — 88/100, range 87–89. Rock solid.

Then the benchmark did its real job — it broke things and showed me why:
→ It caught two bugs in my gateway, not the models: GPT-5 rejects the old max_tokens param, and the Gemini SDK throws on truncated replies. Both were silently failing every call. No happy-path demo would've shown me that.
→ It ran me into the limits of the pipeline: a fresh OpenAI key with no billing, Gemini's free tier exhausting under repeated runs.

THE LESSON
Reliability isn't just model quality. It's the whole pipeline — parameters, quotas, rate limits, retries — holding up under real conditions. A model you can't call reliably is unreliable, full stop.

GPT and Gemini scores drop in once I sort provider billing. But the point was never the ranking. The point is: test your agents, or your users will.

Live board 👉 lancimoun.github.io/agent-reliability-arena/#leaderboard

I build AI systems that are tested, not just demoed. If that's what your AI product needs — my DMs are open.

#AI #ArtificialIntelligence #LLM #AIAgents #GenerativeAI #LLMOps #AIEngineering #BuildInPublic #AIReliability

text:
Hey guys,

I built speedinvoices.com — a fast, no-friction invoice app for sending invoices to your clients. If you've been reaching for the usual free invoicing tools, this is worth a look.

It's grown a lot since I launched it last week. The biggest addition is a Pro plan that lets you save and sync your invoices to your account across devices. But if you care about privacy, the free version is free forever — invoices stay only on the device/browser where you created them. Nothing is uploaded unless you choose to.

New to it? Here's the quick guide: https://speedinvoices.com/how-to

Why Pro is great if you invoice regularly (say you're a nomad/freelancer billing clients every month around the 15th or 30th):

- Recurring invoices — set a schedule and we generate + email each invoice automatically on the cadence you pick.

- Dynamic email content — write your subject and message once with {{ }} placeholders like {{ today }}, {{ client }}, {{ invoice_number }}, or {{ period_start }}, and they fill in with real values every time it sends. They're timezone-aware (so a late-night {{ today }} doesn't drift to the wrong day), and you get autocomplete + a live preview as you type. More here: https://speedinvoices.com/email-variables

- Attachments — include extra files with the invoice.

- A heads-up the day before — so you can tweak the email or add attachments before it actually goes out.

- Prefer to stay hands-on? Choose "I'll send it myself" and we email the finished invoice to you — a reminder to forward it to your client yourself.

- Send from your own domain — e.g. mine goes out from invoice@harlekoy.dev, so the invoice looks professional and on-brand.

- A library of invoice templates to choose from.

Pricing's here: https://speedinvoices.com/pricing

And again — it's free forever for quick one-off invoices, with optional cloud sync when you register so you can pick up your invoices on any device.

Try it now. 🙏

DOST-PAGASA officials launch the PANaHON (PAGASA National Hydro-Met Observing Network) Mobile App during a press conference held in observance of Typhoon and Flood Awareness Week (TFAW) at the PAGASA Science Garden in Quezon City on Monday, June 15.

The PANaHON mobile app is the official smartphone application of DOST-PAGASA. It provides Filipinos with real-time weather data, radar imagery, and location-based alerts. The app combines PAGASA observations with gridded ECMWF forecasts for high spatial accuracy.

📷: Santi San Juan | MB

Hey devs! 👋

Just finished building Eskwela — an AI-powered student scheduler for Filipino students.

Core features:

📸 AI schedule scanner (photo → auto-input)

🔔 Class reminders

📱 Home screen widget

⌚ Smartwatch support

📝 Assignment & PT reminders

Built with Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, Supabase backend, Groq AI.

Now entering Google Play closed testing — need 12 active Android testers for 14 days.

Testers get a FREE premium account (no ads). 🌟

DM me or comment if you're in! 🐧

text:
What started as a random boredom project yesterday turned into something I'm genuinely excited about. 📸✨

Introducing my vintage photobooth web app designed to recreate the magic of classic photobooths right from your phone.

Create timeless photo strips and Polaroid-style prints with an experience inspired by real vintage photobooths.

But my favorite feature? ❤️

**Duet Booth** — a way for two people to create memories together, even when they're miles apart. The idea came from being away from my partner and wishing we could still step into the same photobooth together.

And the best part?

✨ Completely **FREE** to use
✨ **No sign-up or login required**
✨ **No photos are saved online or in the cloud** — your privacy comes first

Just open the link, capture memories, and enjoy the experience.

Because distance shouldn't stop us from making memories.

🔗 [https://booth.stoodioph.com/](https://booth.stoodioph.com/)

#VintagePhotobooth #DuetBooth #MadeWithLove #NoSignUp #PrivacyFirst

Hello Builders! Im building Ztamp Digital Loyalty, a digital loyalty and ordering utility designed for local micro-merchants (cafes, barbershops, nail salon, flower shops, etc.). Currently we are over 300 users and helping businesses get repeat customers. 

How it works:
* A customer visits your physical store or clicks your custom [https://ztamp.it/](https://ztamp.it/) link on social media.
* Every time they buy a coffee, service, or product, they receive a unique code to log their digital stamp.
* Instead of carrying multiple paper cards or downloading separate apps, customers track all their active stamps across different local shops from a single, unified dashboard.

text:
Good day everyone!

As a graduating student, one of the many things that greatly helped me in my professional journey are hackathons. Not only did it give me new experience and knowledge, it also honed what I already have. It gave me confidence, competency, and an opportunity to showcase my team's ideas.

Now that I am employed, I can vouch that the experience gained from these events really helped me in keeping up with the industry. And as someone who is now mentoring some of my juniors, I always encourage them to participate in such activities.

However, starting in hackathon can be quite troublesome. Based on experience, it was very difficult to find or get a gist of these events. Most of the hackathon announcements were being posted on platforms that are algorithm-based which makes it very hard to find for someone that will just start their hackathon journey. Moreover, most hackathons seems daunting for newcomers which is why I believe a filter for beginner-friendly hackathons will surely help a lot.

With that, a collaboration between me, Clarenz Mauro, and Ed Hernandez brings you Hack-A-Ton, a hackathon listing platform aiming to encourage hackathon visibility. Our main goal is not only to become a platform, but a trigger for future students to try these events out and explore. Thank you.

Visit the link: https://hack-a-ton-lac.vercel.app

If you have any recommendations or suggestions for enhancements in our v1. Just comment down below.

And if you are a hackathon organizer or you might know someone who is, you can use our platform as an additional option as we expand its audience.

**Lasso — Circle to Search, but for Mac**

Hi App Builders PH! 👋

I wanted to share a side project I've been building over the past few days.

As someone who uses Google Lens and Circle to Search constantly on Android, I always wished I had something similar on my Mac.

**Lasso **lets you capture anything on your screen and then:

• Extract text using on-device OCR

• Translate text instantly

• Ask AI questions about the captured content

• Use Apple Intelligence, Ollama, MLX local models, or your own cloud model

As a developer, I find it especially useful for copying text from images, extracting code snippets, and asking questions about them directly inside the app—all while keeping everything local when using on-device models.

For anyone interested to try I'll paste the below.

text:
Struggling to stay on top of your daily goals?

 🚀 I’ve been coding non-stop for the past 3 days to bring this passion project to life. It’s finally time to share a first look at Dayflow!
​This isn't just another tracker. To build this, I’m utilizing NativePHP, a "newborn" framework that is rapidly changing the game. It allows me to leverage the power of PHP to build rich, native applications without needing to jump to entirely different languages.

 ​The development experience has been incredible, especially with my Antigrav + Claude setup. Using AI-assisted workflows to build and iterate on the architecture has made the development process feel like a leap into the future. It’s amazing to see how these cutting-edge tools can turn complex logic into such a clean, intuitive experience in such a short time.

 ​I am still actively refining the features and the flow, so I am very much open to your honest criticism and suggestions in the comments! Let me know what you think of the design or the functionality.

​#AppDevelopment #NativePHP #PHP #SoftwareEngineering #BuildInPublic #Dayflow #ProductivityTools #CodingLife #UIUXDesign #Innovation

Hi guys! I just wanted to share an app I made. It’s a cute and simple self-care routine tracker with themed widgets, designed especially with women in mind.

My goal was to keep the app gentle, focused, and not overwhelming. That’s why the habit list is limited to a maximum of 5 habits, so users can focus on a few meaningful routines instead of feeling pressured to track too many things at once.

I also added streaks and reminders to help users stay motivated and consistent with their daily self-care routines.

The app isn’t free, but I’d really appreciate any ideas, feedback, or suggestions on what I can add or improve based on the screenshots attached to this post. Thanks!

I just would like to share the SaaS that i developed for the past few months. It is called “ServiceFlow”, it is a multi-tenant business management system targeted for businesses that has booking system, like Salon, beauty clinic, spa, etc;

the idea is simple, its a business management system and also a booking system, but instead of just that, the system also helps the business retain its customer and have more.

some of its features are:

✅ Public booking page for each business
✅ Online booking flow with available time slots
✅ Owner dashboard for revenue, bookings, staff, reminders, and queue
✅ Service/package/voucher/sale event management
✅ Customer records and booking history
✅ Staff attendance and payroll workflows
✅ Reports and smart insights
✅ Growth/sales opportunity suggestions
✅ Social media post and caption generation for promotions

One feature I’m really excited about is the growth/social media side. For example, if the system detects open slots or possible slow days, it can suggest a sales opportunity and help generate a promotional post that the business can use for Facebook or other social platforms.

text:
Hi everyone!

I recently launched the open beta of Billnox - a work tracking, client reporting, and invoicing app I started building because I needed it myself as a freelancer/dev.

So I built Billnox to make that workflow cleaner.

What makes it different is hindi lang siya basic time tracker.

With Billnox, freelancers can:

-Track billable work and tasks
- Generate invoices from tracked work
- Handle different currencies per client/invoice
- Share real-time progress reports with clients
- Give clients a workspace link without requiring them to log in
- Let clients view updates, reports, invoices, and send requests/messages in one place

The goal is simple: help freelancers make their work more transparent, easier to explain, and easier to bill.

I’m sharing it here because it’s now in open beta, and I want to see if Billnox can also help other freelancers, developers, VAs, creatives, and service providers who deal with client work and billing.

Would appreciate feedback from fellow builders and freelancers.

You can try it here: https://billnox.com

Still early, but actively improving it based on real freelancer feedback. 🙏

Over the last few months, I’ve been quietly building a mobile workout application called LiftLogic. I designed it to be a clean, distraction-free space to track workouts, organize routines, and safely monitor joint health and recovery. 

Building the app is only half the puzzle, though. What I care about most is making sure it’s genuinely helpful to real people—no matter where they are on their fitness journey. 

That's why I’m putting together a small beta testing group (around 5 to 15 people). I’m intentionally looking for a diverse mix of backgrounds to try it out together:

✨ Complete beginners who have never touched a dumbbell before and want a friendly, non-intimidating start.

✨ Casual gym-goers looking for consistency and a simple tool to keep them on track.

✨ Experienced lifters who love tracking progression, geeking out over training stats, and managing recovery.

No matter your experience level, your perspective is incredibly valuable to me. There’s no high pressure here—just use the app at your own pace for a few weeks, and we can chat once a week about how it feels on the gym floor. Whether you need an encouraging hand to guide you or just a friend to review your lifting stats and training data with, I’m here for it.

If you’d like to join our mixed testing group, try out the app, or just connect to talk about your fitness goals, please fill out this quick 1-minute form! 

Thank you so much for the support, and I can’t wait to build this together. 🙏

SukliPH — build in public update
Quick update from what we’re building with SukliPH

The core idea

SukliPH is basically a combination of a calculator and a notebook for #sarisaristore and small retailers

1. Auto sukli calculation

Instantly calculates change during transactions, so store owners don’t have to do mental math or pull out a separate calculator.

2. Daily sales tracking

Acts like a simple digital ledger to record sales throughout the day and keep totals organized.

Why this matters

A lot of micro-business owners still rely on handwritten notebooks and manual calculations. That works — until transactions pile up, numbers get messy, or you need to review sales later.

We’re trying to remove that friction without making the app feel complicated.

What’s coming next

We’re currently working on an automated SMS reminder system for “utang” (store credit).

The goal is simple: help store owners follow up on unpaid balances politely and consistently, without manually texting every customer.

A product lesson so far

One thing we keep relearning: features that seem “too simple” are often the ones users care about most. Fast calculations, clear records, and reminders that save a few minutes each day can matter more than flashy dashboards.

Question for builders

If you’re building for offline or non-technical users, what trade-offs do you make between adding features and keeping the product dead simple?

**PTPA**
**Hello everyone!** 👋 Just sharing my mini-side project.

Nakaka-umay din minsan na araw-araw mo nang ginagawa yung parehong routine bago ka makapag-start mag-code.

Open VS Code → open terminal → run php artisan serve → run npm run dev → run Vite → run Python scripts → repeat the next day or every time you accidentally close your IDE. 😅

Dahil doon, gumawa ako ng StackConsole - a desktop app that lets you start all your project's services with a single click.

Instead na isa-isahin mo pa yung mga commands every time, pwede mo silang i-register once and launch everything from one dashboard.

Current features:

• Project lists – group related services per project
• Live Log Streaming – real-time logs without polling delays
• System Tray – minimize to tray while services continue running in the background
• Service Status Indicators – quickly see which services are running and on what ports
• Built-in Terminal – run ad-hoc commands without leaving the app
• Persistent Projects – your commands stay saved after restarts and reinstalls

Works with pretty much any command:

• PHP / Laravel (php artisan serve)
• Node.js (npm run dev)
• Vite
• Python scripts
• Other CLI-based services

This is still in beta/pre-release, so expect bugs, rough edges, and missing or unfinished features.

Some things I'm planning to add:

• Docker support
• Linux & macOS support
• Better logging
• Improved built-in terminal
• Service dependencies/startup order
• More monitoring and automation features

Current resource usage is around 50–70MB RAM, with little to no CPU usage when idle.

Would love to hear your feedback:

• What features would make this useful for your workflow?
• What would stop you from using it?
• What should I prioritize next?

Download (Beta):
🔗 [[https://github.com/tionic929/stack-console-v2/releases](https://github.com/tionic929/stack-console-v2/releases)](https://github.com/tionic929/stack-console-v2/releases)

Thanks, and feel free to roast the UI, suggest features, or report bugs. 🙏

Hello everyone! I’m excited to showcase my second mobile application I developed, **Spillr**.

I’ve been amazed by how many developers in this group have been sharing their own impressive applications, from trackers, productivity, management and etc. tools to many other useful apps. Seeing those projects inspired me to create something in a different direction, so I decided to explore the **Entertainment** category.

**Spillr **brings the energy of icebreaker card games into your pocket, making every hangout, team gathering, or first meeting a little more memorable.

**Here’s how it works:**
Flip through question decks, choose to answer or skip, and see your results at the end of each round. Simple, fun, and surprisingly entertaining.

**What makes Spillr different:**
* Multiple question decks across different conversation styles

sharedPost.text:
PISOWISE — para sa mga Pinoy na pagod nang habulin kung saan napupunta ang sweldo.

I know what you're thinking — "another finance tracker app?" Yes, marami na nyan. Honestly, I doubted this idea myself at first. Akala ko, sino pa ba ang gagamit ng isa pang tracker? But the more I looked at my own gastos — and how hard it's gotten to save these days — the more I realized people don't need another complicated app. They need one that actually fits how we live. So I kept building.

Ang hirap kasi mag-ipon ngayon. Prices keep going up — bigas, kuryente, pamasahe — and by the end of the month, parang naglaho lang ang pera. I built Pisowise exactly for that problem. Hindi para pigilan kang gumastos, but so you can actually see where your money goes.

One thing na mahalaga sa akin — it works fully offline. No need for constant data or wifi. Ma-log mo ang gastos mo kahit nasa palengke ka, nasa byahe, o kahit walang signal. Local-first talaga ang build, so your records stay with you and your money info stays private sa device mo lang.

Here's the part I'm most proud of — I made tracking your money feel less like a chore and more like a game. Most people quit after a few days kasi nakakaumay. So in Pisowise, you build daily streaks every time you log, earn badges for hitting milestones like your first ₱1,000 saved or paying down a debt, and gain XP just for staying consistent. May guided money journeys din — emergency fund, first investment, debt payoff — kaya may sense of progress ka talaga. Para mong nilalaro ang savings mo, except totoo ang panalo.

And of course, it has Piso AI — just type what you spent, like "350 lunch sa Jollibee," and it logs it for you automatically. It's powered by Apple Intelligence, so it's fast, smart, and runs right on your device. Everything's in one app too — budgets, goals, debts, bills, groceries, investments, even split bills kapag naghatian kayo ng barkada. It's PHP-first, built around how Filipinos actually handle money.

But more than that, here's my real goal: to help Filipinos track their spending now that everything's getting more expensive. And I'm not stopping with this one — I'll keep building apps that solve the real, everyday problems our community deals with. Isa lang ito sa marami pang gusto kong gawin para sa kapwa Pinoy.

Now, full disclosure — hindi pa ito published. Wala pa ito sa App Store. Right now I'm only opening it to a small, whitelisted group of beta testers — meaning kailangan ko muna ang email mo para ma-add kita sa access list bago mo magamit ang app. This is your chance to get in early, try it before everyone else, and help me shape it before the official launch.

So kung gusto mong maging isa sa mga first users, comment ka lang dito or send me a message with your email para ma-whitelist kita. Limited slots lang talaga, so whoever responds first gets in first.

Take note that this is only for iOS devices and if this app goes boom! I will develop also for Android Users.

https://pisowise.vercel.app/
